element.name: Customs Legislation on Governance Interoperability (EBI)
element.documentation:
Definition: Customs Legislation on Governance Interoperability (EBI) is a grouping that covers various regulations and directives issued by the European Union. These regulations pertain to mutual recognition of protection measures in civil matters, the Union Customs Code, and market surveillance and compliance of products.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Customs Legislation on Governance Interoperability (EBI) includes key regulations such as Regulation (EU) No 606/2013, which deals with mutual recognition of protection measures in civil matters. It also includes Regulation (EU) No 952/2013, which lays down the Union Customs Code. Another important regulation in this grouping is Regulation (EU) 2019/1020, which pertains to market surveillance and compliance of products. These regulations are crucial for ensuring smooth and compliant trade within the European Union.
Example: Regulation (EU) No 606/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 12 June 2013 on mutual recognition of protection measures in civil matters This regulation ensures that protection measures taken in one EU country are recognized and maintained in any other EU countries to which a person moves or travels.
Regulation (EU) No 952/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 9 October 2013 laying down the Union Customs Code This regulation provides a framework for customs rules and procedures in the EU customs territory, adapted to modern trade realities and modern communication tools.
Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 on market surveillance and compliance of products Article 4 This regulation outlines the tasks of economic operators regarding products subject to certain Union harmonisation legislation.

element.name: Customs Legislation on Structural Interoperability (ENBI)
element.documentation:
Definition: Customs Legislation on Structural Interoperability (ENBI) ABB is a grouping that covers the legal, technical, and procedural elements that facilitate the exchange of information and data between different customs systems. It includes the laws, regulations, standards, and protocols that ensure seamless communication and data exchange between disparate customs systems, thereby promoting efficient customs operations and compliance with international trade laws.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The ENBI ABB is crucial in the context of international trade as it ensures that different customs systems can effectively communicate and exchange data. This is particularly important given the increasing digitalization of customs operations and the growing complexity of international trade laws. The ENBI ABB covers a wide range of elements, including legal provisions that govern data exchange between customs systems, technical standards that ensure the compatibility of different systems, and procedural guidelines that facilitate efficient data exchange. By promoting structural interoperability, the ENBI ABB contributes to the overall efficiency and effectiveness of customs operations.
Example: An example of application of the ENBI ABB could be the implementation of a new data exchange protocol between two countries' customs systems. This would involve not only the technical aspects of establishing the data link, but also the legal and procedural elements, such as ensuring compliance with data protection laws and establishing procedures for data verification and validation.

element.name: Legislation on Governance Interoperability (EBI)
element.documentation:
Definition: Legislation on Governance Interoperability (EBI) is a grouping that covers a range of directives and regulations enacted by the European Parliament and Council. These legislative instruments aim to harmonize and modernize various sectors including electronic communications, digital content and services, public procurement, insurance distribution, payment services, cross-border parcel delivery services, cross-border payments, geo-blocking, and electronic commerce within the European Union (EU). The purpose of these legislations is to promote transparency, competition, innovation, consumer protection, and fair trade practices across the EU's internal market.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The EBI catalogue includes various directives and regulations that govern different sectors within the EU. These legislative instruments have been enacted with the aim of harmonizing rules and regulations across member states, promoting competition and innovation, protecting consumer rights, and ensuring fair trade practices. They cover a wide range of areas including electronic communications, digital content and services, public procurement, insurance distribution, payment services, cross-border parcel delivery services, cross-border payments, geo-blocking, and electronic commerce. Each legislation has specific objectives and requirements that must be adhered to by the relevant stakeholders.
Example: For instance, Directive (EU) 2018/1972, also known as the European Electronic Communications Code, modernizes and harmonizes the regulatory framework for electronic communications across the EU. On the other hand, Directive (EU) 2019/770 focuses on contracts for the provision of digital content and digital services, aiming to strengthen consumer rights in the digital market. Similarly, Regulation (EU) 2018/302, known as the Geo-blocking Regulation, addresses unjustified geo-blocking and other forms of discrimination based on customers' nationality or location within the internal market.

element.name: Business Agnostic Messaging Solutions
element.documentation:
Description: Messaging Solutions ABB is a grouping that refers to actual solutions that facilitate the exchange of information through digital messages. These solutions can include email, SMS, instant messaging, push notifications, and other forms of digital communication. They are designed to streamline and simplify the process of sending, receiving, and managing messages in a digital environment.
Additional information: Messaging solutions are an integral part of modern communication, especially in business environments. They can be used for a variety of purposes, including customer service, marketing, internal communication, and more. These solutions often include features like automation, personalization, analytics, and integration with other systems. They can be used to send messages to individuals or groups, and can support various types of content, including text, images, videos, and links. Messaging solutions can also include security features to protect the privacy and integrity of the messages.
Example: Examples of messaging solutions include email marketing platforms like MailChimp, customer service chatbots, internal communication tools like Slack, and SMS marketing services. These solutions can be used in a variety of contexts. For example, a business might use an email marketing platform to send promotional messages to customers, a chatbot to answer customer inquiries, and an internal communication tool to facilitate communication among employees.

element.name: Business Agnostic Identity Management Solutions
element.documentation:
Description: Bussiness Agnostic Identity Management Solutions (BAIMS) is a grouping that refers to actual solutions that facilitate the management of user identities across various business models and industries. These solutions are designed to be flexible and adaptable, allowing businesses of any type or size to effectively manage user access, authentication, and security.
Additional information: BAIMS are crucial in today's digital age where security and privacy are of utmost importance. They provide a comprehensive approach to managing the identities of users in an organization, regardless of the nature of the business. They are designed to handle tasks such as user authentication, authorization, roles and access management, password management, policy enforcement, and audit and reporting. These solutions are not tied to a specific business model or industry, making them versatile and adaptable. They can be integrated with various systems and platforms, providing a seamless user experience while ensuring security and compliance.
Example: Examples of application of BAIMS include: 1) In a healthcare setting, these solutions can be used to manage the identities of doctors, nurses, and patients, ensuring that only authorized individuals have access to sensitive patient data. 2) In a retail business, they can be used to manage the identities of customers and employees, facilitating secure transactions and protecting customer information. 3) In a financial institution, they can be used to manage the identities of account holders and employees, ensuring secure access to financial data and systems.

element.name: Legislation on Behavioural Interoperability (NBI)
element.documentation:
Definition: Legislation on Behavioural Interoperability (NBI) is a grouping that covers a set of laws, regulations, and guidelines aimed at ensuring the seamless interaction of different systems, applications, and services. It focuses on the behavior of systems when they interact, ensuring that they operate together effectively and efficiently. The NBI legislation is designed to facilitate the exchange of information and services among different systems, promoting interoperability and integration.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Legislation on Behavioural Interoperability (NBI) is an important aspect of information technology and telecommunications. It is concerned with the ability of different systems, applications, and services to work together seamlessly. This involves not only the technical aspects of interoperability but also the legal and regulatory aspects. The NBI legislation provides a framework for ensuring that systems behave in a predictable and consistent manner when they interact, facilitating the exchange of information and services. It covers a wide range of areas, including data exchange standards, communication protocols, interface specifications, and service level agreements.
Example: An example of the application of the Legislation on Behavioural Interoperability (NBI) is in the healthcare sector. Here, different systems such as electronic health records, hospital information systems, and telemedicine applications need to interact seamlessly to provide effective and efficient healthcare services. The NBI legislation ensures that these systems can exchange information and services in a predictable and consistent manner, promoting interoperability and integration.

element.name: Customs Reference Data
element.documentation:
Definition: Customs Reference Data is a grouping that covers a comprehensive set of elements related to customs procedures and regulations. It includes information on customs offices, product classification codes, country codes, currency codes, units of measure, legal references, and customs valuation methods. These elements are essential for ensuring compliance with customs requirements and procedures, facilitating international trade, and enabling unambiguous electronic communication of quantities together with their units.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Customs Reference Data catalogue includes elements such as the Reference Data Customs Offices List, which provides information on the Reference Data (RD) and the Customs Office List (COL) used by national customs applications. It also includes the Harmonized System (HS) Codes, an internationally standardized system for classifying products and goods. The ISO Country Codes, which are internationally recognized codes that designate every country and most of the dependent areas, are also part of this catalogue. The catalogue also includes the Currency Code List, the Unified Code for Units of Measure (UCUM), Legal and Regulatory References, and Customs Valuation Methods.
Example: For instance, the Harmonized System (HS) Codes are used to determine the customs duties, taxes, and regulations applicable to specific products during import or export. Similarly, the ISO Country Codes are used in top-level domains on the Internet and at international events. The Currency Code List is used to list concepts associated with currencies and currency subunits, while the Unified Code for Units of Measure (UCUM) is used to facilitate unambiguous electronic communication of quantities together with their units.

element.name: Business Agnostic Dataset Solutions
element.documentation: Narrative: The "Semantic view - Business Agnostic Datasets" viewpoint extends organizational view and provides a comprehensive framework for managing and utilizing business agnostic datasets within the digital ecosystem. This view associates the Agnostic Datasets with the Business Information Base and Digital Public Services from the application layer. Within this view, Agnostic Datasets represent standardized collections of data that are independent of specific business domains. These datasets adhere to common data structures, formats, and semantics, enabling interoperability, data integration, and efficient data exchange across different digital services and applications. The Business Information Base, as part of the application layer, serves as a repository of business-related information that utilizes the Agnostic Datasets. It stores and manages domain-specific data within the standardized dataset structures, facilitating data consistency, accessibility, and sharing. Digital Public Services leverage the Agnostic Datasets to ensure uniformity and coherence in data representation and utilization. These services align their data models, operations, and interactions with the agnostic datasets, enabling seamless integration, data consistency, and semantic interoperability among different digital public services. By associating the Agnostic Datasets with the Business Information Base and Digital Public Services, the "Semantic view - Business Agnostic Datasets" promotes standardized data management practices and efficient data utilization within the digital ecosystem. This view supports data integration, semantic interoperability, and advanced functionalities for digital public services. The agnostic nature of the datasets allows for flexibility and adaptability across different business domains and digital public services. It enables reusability of data structures, reduces data duplication, and promotes consistent data representation and exchange.

element.name: Business Agnostic Metadata Catalogue Solutions
element.documentation:
Definition: NARRATIVE:The 'Business Agnostic Metadata Catalogue' in ArchiMate is a grouping that organizes various elements based on their concerns or responsibilities. In the provided JSON, there are three main elements: [JRC Data Catalogue], [SV-Metadata Catalogue], and [Smart Data Models]. 1. [JRC Data Catalogue]: This is a Data Object SBB type element. It represents the Joint Research Center (JRC) Data Catalogue, which is a collection of metadata records providing information about datasets produced by the JRC. The JRC, as the European Commission's in-house science service, conducts research to provide independent scientific advice and support to the policies of the European Union. This element does not contain any sub-elements.2. [SV-Metadata Catalogue]: This is an Archimate Diagram-model ABB type element. The description is not provided in the JSON, but based on its type, it can be inferred that this element represents a metadata catalogue in the form of an ArchiMate diagram model. This element also does not contain any sub-elements.3. [Smart Data Models]: This is another Data Object SBB type element. It represents a smart data model, which includes three elements: the schema (technical representation of the model defining the technical data types and structure), the specification (a written document for human readers), and the examples of the payloads for NGSIv2 and NGSI-LD versions. This element also does not contain any sub-elements.In the context of ArchiMate's grouping, these elements are catalogued in the 'Business Agnostic Metadata Catalogue' based on their responsibilities or concerns, which revolve around data and metadata management, research, and policy support.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The BAMS catalogue includes the JRC Data Catalogue, a collection of metadata records detailing datasets produced by the Joint Research Centre (JRC) in line with its Data Policy. The JRC, the European Commission's in-house science service, conducts research to provide independent scientific advice and support to EU policies. Another key element in the catalogue is Smart Data Models. These models include a schema (technical representation of the model defining the technical data types and structure), a specification (written document for human readers), and examples of the payloads for NGSIv2 and NGSI-LD versions. These models are 'smart' because they are designed to be easily understood and used by both humans and machines, facilitating more effective data management and utilization.

element.name: Customs Legislation on Behavioural Interoperability (ENBI)
element.documentation:
Definition: Customs Legislation on Behavioural Interoperability (ENBI) ABB is a grouping that covers the set of rules, regulations, and standards that govern the interaction of different systems and processes in the customs domain. It aims to ensure seamless and efficient communication and data exchange between various customs systems and stakeholders.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The ENBI catalogue is designed to facilitate the interoperability of customs systems at a behavioural level. It encompasses all the legislative elements that dictate how these systems should interact, communicate, and exchange data. This includes, but is not limited to, laws, regulations, standards, and guidelines. The purpose of this catalogue is to ensure that all customs systems, regardless of their individual characteristics or the country in which they operate, can work together seamlessly and efficiently. This is crucial for facilitating international trade, preventing customs fraud, and ensuring the security of international supply chains.
Example: Examples of application for the ENBI catalogue could include the standardization of data formats for customs declarations, the development of common protocols for the exchange of customs data between different countries, or the establishment of guidelines for the integration of new technologies into existing customs systems.
LOST view: LV-Architecture Principles

element.name: Data Space Policies and Contracts
element.documentation:
Definition: Data Space Policies and Contracts ABB is a grouping that covers two primary elements: Data Policy and Data Contract. These elements are integral to the management and governance of data within an organization or system, outlining the rules, regulations, and agreements that dictate how data is handled, shared, and used.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Data Policy element within this grouping refers to the set of rules and guidelines established by an organization or system to manage its data, ensuring its quality, accessibility, and protection. This includes policies on data collection, storage, processing, distribution, and disposal. On the other hand, the Data Contract element refers to the formal agreement between parties on the terms and conditions of data sharing and usage. This includes the rights and responsibilities of each party, the scope of data to be shared, the purpose of data sharing, and the measures for data security and privacy. Together, these elements form the foundation of a robust data governance framework, enabling organizations to effectively manage their data assets while ensuring compliance with relevant laws and regulations.
Example: An example of a Data Policy could be a company's policy on data privacy, which outlines the measures it takes to protect the personal data of its customers, such as encryption and anonymization techniques. An example of a Data Contract could be an agreement between a healthcare provider and a research institution, where the provider agrees to share patient data for research purposes, under the condition that the data is de-identified to protect patient privacy.
LOST view: SV-Agnostic Data Policies and Contracts- Data Space

element.name: Test Enablers
element.documentation:
Definition: Test Enablers ABB is a Grouping that refers to the applications and services that support the development and deployment of conformance testing and validation.
Source: Inspired in European Comision
Source reference: https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/testing-and-experimentation-facilities-tefs-questions-and-answers
Example: The following implementation is an example on how this specific Architecture Building Block (ABB) can be instantiated as a Solution Building Block (SBB): Interoperability Testbed - The Test Bed allows users to execute predefined test cases on their systems in order to test the conformance to standards and requirements, simulate a web-service, validate content and test a complete message exchange protocol. The Testbed manages test cases and users, and orchestrates domain-specific components, the domain-specific logic is in separate components that are used via web services. Test results are provided in a standardised, machine-readable format. The Test Bed also offers a test registry and repository (TRR) to store test artefacts (assertions, test cases, validation schemas, etc.) and compile test services (validation services, simulator services, etc.). Please visit the following website for more information: https://ec.europa.eu/isa2/solutions/interoperability-test-bed_en
Interoperability Dimension: Governance IoP
LOST view: Technical view - application
Interoperability Saliency: The Test Enablers Grouping ABB is salient for interoperability because testing and validation solutions services are relevant aspects to ensure that they are conformant to relevant standards enabling interoperability.

element.name: Business Agnostic Digital Business Capabilities Map
element.documentation:
Definition: Business Agnostic Digital Business Capabilities Catalogue ABB is a Grouping that refers to the actual catalogue of digital business capabilities (DBC) that puts together a range of capabilities related to various digital business operations. These capabilities are crucial for organizations to effectively and efficiently manage their digital operations, gain valuable insights, make informed decisions, ensure data quality, security, and compliance, and generate value and revenue.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The catalogue includes a wide range of capabilities such as Electronic Identification, Qualification Management, Digital Payments, Digital Procurement, Digital Communication, Digital Exchange, Digital Invoicing, Data Management, Multimedia Management, Contact Management, Case and Workflow Management, Knowledge Management, Digital Twin, Artificial Intelligence, and Business Agnostic Data Management Digital Business Capability Catalogue. Each of these capabilities has a specific role and function in the digital business operations of an organization. For instance, Electronic Identification ensures secure access to online services, Digital Payments enables the purchase of goods or services via digital modes, and Data Management is responsible for the development, execution, and supervision of plans, policies, programs, and practices that deliver, control, protect, and enhance the value of data and information assets throughout their lifecycles.
Example: An example of the application of these capabilities can be seen in a digital business operation where Electronic Identification is used to ensure secure access to online services, Digital Payments are used to facilitate the purchase of goods or services, Digital Communication is used for virtual collaboration, and Data Management is used to manage and enhance the value of data and information assets. Similarly, in the Business Agnostic Data Management Digital Business Capability Catalogue, capabilities such as Data Discovery, Data Analytics, Data Monetization, Data Governance, Data Ethics, Data Interoperability, Data Sharing, Data Quality, Data Security, and Data Lineage are used to effectively and efficiently manage data assets, gain valuable insights, make informed decisions, ensure data quality, security, and compliance, and generate value and revenue.
LOST view: OV-Data Spaces

element.name: Business Agnostic Business Information Base
element.documentation:
Definition: Business Agnostic Business Information Base (ABB) is a grouping that refers to the actual catalogue of information entities that covers a wide range of business-related elements. These elements include payments, transactions, identification, qualifications, audit trails, access rights, profiles, messages, availability, digital signatures, documents, security measures, locations, invoices, contracting authorities, economic operators, digital assets, credentials, data quality, and distribution lists.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Business Agnostic Business Information Base (ABB) is a comprehensive catalogue of information entities that are applicable across various business domains. It includes elements such as 'Payment' which refers to the voluntary tendering of money or its equivalent, 'Transaction' which is an interaction of individuals/entities with outside entities, 'Identification' which is data that could potentially be used to identify a particular person or entity, and 'Qualification' which is something that could potentially be used to qualify a particular person or entity. Other elements like 'Audit trail', 'Access rights', 'Profile', 'Message', 'Availability', 'Digital Signature', 'Document', 'Security Measure', 'Location', 'Invoice', 'Contracting authority', 'Economic operator', 'Digital Asset', 'Credential', 'Data Quality', and 'Distribution list' are also part of this catalogue, each with its own specific definition and purpose.
Example: For instance, in a financial institution, the 'Payment' element would refer to the transactions made by customers, 'Identification' would refer to the customer's personal information, 'Access rights' would determine what information a customer or employee can view, 'Digital Signature' would be used to verify the authenticity of digital messages or documents, and 'Data Quality' would refer to the state of qualitative or quantitative pieces of information within the institution.
LOST view: OV-Functional Architecture Principles

element.name: Customs Risk Management and Analysis Enablers
element.documentation:
Definition: Customs Risk Management and Analysis Enablers ABB is a Grouping that covers digital solutions and methodologies used in the systematic assessment and evaluation of potential risks associated with trade transactions and customs operations. It involves the use of data analytics, algorithms, and risk management methodologies to identify patterns, anomalies, and potential risks in real-time.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The elements within this grouping are designed to enhance the efficiency of customs authorities by enabling them to prioritize inspections, allocate resources effectively, and mitigate risks related to smuggling, fraud, security threats, and non-compliance. They leverage factors such as shipment details, trader profiles, country of origin, and historical data to provide a comprehensive risk analysis. This supports informed decision-making and ensures effective risk management within the customs domain.
Example: Risk analysis Risk analysis is a key element within the Customs Risk Management and Analysis Enablers grouping. It refers to the systematic assessment and evaluation of potential risks associated with trade transactions and customs operations. By analyzing factors such as shipment details, trader profiles, country of origin, and historical data, risk analysis enables customs authorities to prioritize inspections, allocate resources effectively, and mitigate risks related to smuggling, fraud, security threats, and non-compliance. This digital solution service enhances customs efficiency, facilitates secure trade, and supports informed decision-making to ensure effective risk management within the customs domain.

These developments call into question a number of regulatory matters and pose new questions for national and European-level regulators. (https://www.intereconomics.eu/contents/year/2017/number/1/article/regulating-the-european-sharing-economy-state-of-play-and-challenges.html).

Additional information: The degree of achievement could range from an ideal perfect shared legal framework (i.e. no interoperability barriers from the legal perspective) to an imperfect or even null shared legal framework (i.e. some interoperability barriers from the legal perspective). Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Digital Solution Non-Functional Requirements Catalogue ABB includes various elements such as Extensibility, Observability, Security, Agility, Resiliency, Consistency, Scalability, Availability, Usability, and Durability. Each of these elements has a specific role and importance in the overall system design and operation. For instance, Extensibility refers to the system's ability to accommodate future changes or additions seamlessly, while Observability refers to the system's ability to monitor and analyze its behavior in real-time. Similarly, Security refers to the system's ability to protect itself against unauthorized access and data breaches, while Agility refers to the system's ability to adapt quickly to changing business needs or market conditions. The catalogue also includes various sub-elements under each main element, providing a comprehensive list of non-functional requirements for digital solutions.
Example: An example of applying the Digital Solution Non-Functional Requirements Catalogue ABB could be during the design and development of a new digital banking application. The developers would need to consider various non-functional requirements such as Security (to protect users' financial information), Availability (to ensure the app is always accessible), Usability (to ensure the app is user-friendly), Scalability (to handle increasing number of users), and Extensibility (to easily add new features in the future). Additionally, they would also need to consider sub-elements such as Confidentiality and Integrity under Security, Accessibility and Learnability under Usability, and Disaster Recovery and Recoverability under Resiliency.

element.name: Privacy Data Policy Catalogue
element.documentation:
Definition: Privacy Data Policy Catalogue ABB is a grouping that covers a range of policies and guidelines implemented by an organization to ensure the privacy and protection of personal data. The catalogue includes elements such as the Anonymisation Policy, which outlines the rules and procedures for anonymizing sensitive data in compliance with privacy regulations.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Privacy Data Policy Catalogue ABB is a comprehensive collection of policies and guidelines that an organization uses to safeguard personal data. It includes elements like the Anonymisation Policy, which is a formal document outlining the methods, techniques, and criteria used to transform personally identifiable information (PII) into a form that can no longer be linked to an individual. This policy ensures compliance with privacy regulations and helps mitigate the risk of unauthorized disclosure or misuse of personal data. It includes considerations for data anonymization processes, such as data masking, aggregation, or encryption, to protect individuals' privacy while still allowing data to be used for legitimate business purposes.
Example: An example of an element in the Privacy Data Policy Catalogue ABB is the Anonymisation Policy. This policy could state that all customer data used for internal analytics must first be anonymized through a process of data masking. This would involve replacing identifiable data fields with artificial identifiers or pseudonyms to prevent the identification of individuals. The policy might also specify the use of encryption for data storage and transmission to further protect personal data from unauthorized access or disclosure.

element.name: Customs Data Format, Representation and Syntax Solutions
element.documentation:
Definition: Customs Data Format, Representation and Syntax Solutions ABB is a grouping that covers the specific formats and syntax solutions used for customs declarations. This includes the structures and fields used to capture information about import or export shipments, such as details about goods, their classification, valuation, origin, and other customs-related information.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Customs Data Format, Representation and Syntax Solutions ABB is a comprehensive catalogue of elements that are used in the customs declaration process. These elements are designed to standardize the way information is captured and represented, ensuring that all necessary details are accurately and consistently recorded. This includes information about the goods being imported or exported, their classification according to customs regulations, their valuation, their origin, and any other information that may be relevant to the customs process. The elements in this catalogue are used in various customs declaration formats, including the EDIFACT CUSDEC format.

element.name: Agility Requirements Catalogue
element.documentation:
Definition: Agility Requirements Catalogue ABB is a grouping that covers a set of IT non-functional requirements that contribute to the agility of a software or system. These requirements, including configurability, compatibility, maintainability, and deployability, are crucial for ensuring that the system can adapt to changing needs and environments, can function seamlessly with other systems, can be easily modified and maintained, and can be efficiently deployed and installed.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Agility Requirements Catalogue ABB comprises of four key elements: Configurability, Compatibility, Maintainability, and Deployability. Configurability refers to the system's ability to be easily customized or modified to meet specific needs, without requiring extensive programming knowledge. Compatibility ensures that the system can function properly with other systems, hardware, or environments, and can be easily upgraded or migrated. Maintainability refers to the ease with which the system can be modified, updated, or repaired, contributing to its long-term sustainability. Deployability involves the ease and efficiency with which the software can be deployed and installed on different platforms, reducing downtime and minimizing risk of errors.
Example: An example of the application of the Agility Requirements Catalogue ABB could be in the development of a new software system. The developers would need to ensure that the system is configurable, allowing users to easily customize it to their needs. They would also need to ensure that it is compatible with a range of other systems, software, and hardware to ensure wide usability. The system should be maintainable, with clear documentation and a modular design to allow for easy updates and repairs. Finally, the system should be easily deployable, with a straightforward installation process that minimizes disruption to the existing system.

element.name: Digital Public Service Improvement Principle Catalogue
element.documentation:
Definition: Digital Public Service Improvement Principle Catalogue ABB is a grouping that covers the principles, guidelines, and strategies aimed at enhancing the delivery of public services through digital platforms. The catalogue primarily focuses on the principle of 'Innovation', which is a key driver in the modernization and improvement of public services.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Digital Public Service Improvement Principle Catalogue ABB is an essential tool for public service organizations seeking to leverage digital technologies to improve their service delivery. The catalogue's main element is 'Innovation', which refers to the application of new ideas, methods, or technologies to enhance public service delivery. Innovation in this context can involve the development of new digital services, the improvement of existing services through digital technologies, or the use of digital technologies to create new ways of engaging with the public. The catalogue provides a framework for understanding and applying the principle of innovation in the context of digital public service improvement.
Example: An example of the application of the Digital Public Service Improvement Principle Catalogue ABB could be a local government agency using it as a guide to develop a new online service for residents to report issues in their community. The agency could use the principle of 'Innovation' to explore new ways of receiving and responding to reports, such as through a mobile app or a chatbot, thereby improving the efficiency and accessibility of their service.

element.name: Customs Compliance and Regulatory Requirements Enablers
element.documentation:
Definition: Customs Compliance and Regulatory Requirements Enablers ABB is a Grouping that covers a range of digital platforms and systems designed to streamline, automate, and facilitate the management of customs procedures. These include special, export, transit, and import procedures, as well as the accreditation of Authorised Economic Operators and compliance requirements checks. These systems are aimed at enhancing trade facilitation, ensuring compliance with customs regulations, and promoting efficient and secure cross-border trade within the customs environment.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The elements within the Customs Compliance and Regulatory Requirements Enablers ABB are digital solutions that automate various customs processes such as document verification, risk assessment, and clearance for export and import procedures. They also facilitate electronic communication and data exchange between traders and customs authorities, reducing paperwork, improving accuracy, and expediting procedures. The special procedure element refers to systems managing customs procedures that deviate from standard import/export processes. The transit procedure element refers to systems facilitating the movement of goods under customs control from one customs territory to another. The Authorised Economic Operator accreditation and compliance requirements checks elements, although not described in the provided JSON, likely refer to systems managing the accreditation process for economic operators and ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements.
Example: An example of the application of these elements could be a company using the Export procedure digital solution to electronically submit export declarations and relevant documentation through a centralized online platform. The system would then automate the document verification, risk assessment, and export clearance processes, facilitating electronic communication and data exchange between the company and customs authorities. This would reduce paperwork, improve accuracy, and expedite the export procedure, ensuring compliance with customs regulations and promoting efficient and secure cross-border trade.

element.name: Customs Information Base
element.documentation:
Definition: Customs Information Base ABB is a Grouping that covers a wide range of elements related to customs procedures, regulations, and operations. It includes information on economic operators, customs partners, duties calculation, classification of goods, and more. This information base is crucial for the smooth functioning of customs operations and for ensuring compliance with international trade laws and regulations.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Customs Information Base ABB includes elements such as Economic Operators Registration and Identification number (EORI), free circulation requirement information, laboratories information, threats and fraudulent actions information, duties calculation information, imports information, combined nomenclature, workforce information, classification of goods information, temporary storage information, exports information, special procedures information, binding tariffs information, guarantee information, economic operators information, customs partners information, economic value information, internal logistic information, and origin of goods information. Each of these elements plays a critical role in customs operations, from identifying and registering economic operators to calculating duties and classifying goods. This information base is essential for ensuring that all customs procedures are carried out correctly and efficiently.
Example: For instance, the 'Economic Operators Registration and Identification number (EORI)' element contains information about the EORI, which is a unique identification number that businesses need to import or export goods. The 'Free circulation requirement information' element provides details about the requirements for goods to move freely within a certain area. The 'Laboratories information' element includes data about the laboratories that test the goods for compliance with safety and quality standards. The 'Duties calculation Information' element contains information on how duties on goods are calculated.

element.name: Customs Digital Public Services Catalogue
element.documentation:
Definition: Customs Digital Public Services Catalogue ABB is a Grouping that covers a wide range of digital public services related to customs operations and management. These services include, but are not limited to, Economic Operators Registry management, EU Customs Trader Portal, Analysis Management, Customs logistics management, Centralised Clearance for Import, Determination of the economic value of goods declared for importation, Tariff Registry management, and many others.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Customs Digital Public Services Catalogue ABB encompasses a comprehensive list of digital services that facilitate various customs operations. These services range from managing registries of economic operators and tariffs, to handling customs declarations and duties calculation. They also include digital platforms like the EU Customs Trader Portal, and systems for managing internal customs logistics. Furthermore, the catalogue includes services for compliance verification, partner authorization, and procedure automation. All these services aim to streamline and digitalize customs processes, making them more efficient and accessible.
Example: An example of a service in the Customs Digital Public Services Catalogue is the 'Economic Operators Registry management'. This digital public service is responsible for managing the registry of economic operators. Another example is the 'EU Customs Trader Portal', a digital platform that provides traders with access to various EU customs services. 'Duties calculation and payment' is another service that facilitates the calculation and payment of customs duties.

element.name: Business Agnostic Data Mapping Solutions
element.documentation:
Definition: Business Agnostic Data Mapping Solutions (BADS) is a grouping that covers a range of solutions designed to facilitate the mapping of data from various heterogeneous data structures and serializations to the RDF data model. These solutions are not specific to any particular business or industry, making them versatile and adaptable across different contexts. The key element in this grouping is the RDF Mapping Language (RML), a generic mapping language that extends the W3C-standardized mapping language, R2RML.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Business Agnostic Data Mapping Solutions catalogue primarily includes the RDF Mapping Language (RML), a mapping language that allows for the expression of customized mapping rules from various data structures and serializations to the RDF data model. RML is a superset of R2RML, the W3C standard for expressing customized mappings from relational databases to RDF. As such, RML follows the same syntax as R2RML and extends its applicability and scope by adding support for data in other structured formats. RML mappings are themselves RDF graphs, and this document provides a comprehensive description of the RML language and its concepts through definitions and examples.
Example: An example of the application of Business Agnostic Data Mapping Solutions would be in a scenario where a business needs to map data from a relational database to RDF. Using RML, the business can express customized mapping rules to convert the data from the relational database into the RDF data model. This allows for greater interoperability and flexibility in data management and usage.

element.name: Digital Public Service Operation Principle Catalogue
element.documentation:
Definition: Digital Public Service Operation Principle Catalogue ABB is a grouping that covers a range of principles and guidelines that are essential for the operation of digital public services. These principles include convergence control on public policy goals attainment, data accessibility, data findability, data interoperability, data reusability, preservation of information, security by design, and trust.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Digital Public Service Operation Principle Catalogue ABB is a comprehensive collection of principles that guide the operation of digital public services. 'Convergence control on public policy goals attainment' refers to the alignment of digital services with public policy goals. 'Data Accessibility' and 'Data Findability' pertain to the ease of access and discovery of data respectively. 'Data Interoperability' and 'Data Reusability' concern the ability of systems to work together and the potential for data to be reused. 'Preservation of information' is about maintaining and protecting data, while 'Security by Design' is a principle that emphasizes the importance of incorporating security measures from the onset of system design. Lastly, 'Trust' refers to the confidence and reliability in digital public services.
Example: An example of the application of these principles can be seen in a digital public service like an online tax filing system. The system should be designed with 'Security by Design', ensuring that user data is protected. The data collected should be 'Accessible' and 'Findable' for users, and 'Interoperable' to allow for seamless interaction with other systems. The system should also allow for 'Data Reusability', enabling data to be used for multiple purposes. The 'Preservation of Information' is crucial to maintain historical tax records. The system should also align with the 'Convergence control on public policy goals attainment' by facilitating the efficient collection of taxes. Lastly, the system should foster 'Trust' among users by being reliable and secure.

element.name: National Binding Instruments
element.documentation:
Definition: National Binding Instruments (NBI) is a grouping that covers a broad range of legislative and regulatory frameworks related to interoperability in various domains. This includes structural, behavioural, and governance interoperability. The NBI provides a structured approach to the implementation and management of these frameworks, ensuring that they are in line with national and international standards and best practices.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The National Binding Instruments (NBI) catalogue is a comprehensive repository of legislative and regulatory frameworks that govern interoperability in various domains. It includes the Legislation on Structural Interoperability (NBI), which covers the National Schema on eIdentification, Cybersecurity, eDelivery, and access to Base Registries. It also includes the Legislation on Behavioural Interoperability (NBI) and the Legislation on Governance Interoperability (NBI). Each of these categories contains specific elements that provide detailed information on the respective legislative and regulatory frameworks. The NBI catalogue is designed to facilitate the implementation and management of these frameworks, ensuring compliance with national and international standards and best practices.
Example: For instance, under the Legislation on Structural Interoperability (NBI), there are specific elements such as the National Schema on eIdentification which provides guidelines on electronic identification processes. Similarly, the National Schema on Cybersecurity outlines the legislative framework for managing cybersecurity risks. The National Schema on eDelivery provides the regulatory framework for electronic delivery services, while the National Schema on the access to Base Registries outlines the guidelines for accessing base registries. These elements provide a structured approach to implementing and managing interoperability in their respective domains.
LOST view: LV-Architecture Principles

element.name: Legislation on Governance Interoperability (NNBI)
element.documentation:
Definition: Legislation on Governance Interoperability (NNBI) is a grouping that covers a comprehensive catalogue of information entities related to laws, regulations, and policies that facilitate the interaction between different governance systems. This catalogue is empty as indicated by the JSON provided, but it is intended to house elements that define and describe the legal and regulatory framework that enables interoperability in governance.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Legislation on Governance Interoperability (NNBI) catalogue is designed to be a repository of information entities that detail the legal and regulatory aspects of governance interoperability. Interoperability in this context refers to the ability of different governance systems to work together, exchange information and function effectively. The catalogue is currently empty, but it is intended to include elements such as specific laws, regulations, policies, guidelines, and standards that facilitate interoperability in governance. Each element in the catalogue will have a name and a description, providing a clear understanding of the element's role and relevance in promoting governance interoperability.
Example: An example of an element that might be included in the Legislation on Governance Interoperability (NNBI) catalogue could be a law like the 'Data Sharing and Governance Act'. The name of the element would be 'Data Sharing and Governance Act' and the description might detail how this law facilitates the sharing of data between different governmental departments, thereby promoting interoperability.

element.name: Customs Privacy Data Policy Catalogue
element.documentation:
Definition: Customs Privacy Data Policy Catalogue ABB is a grouping that covers the elements related to the protection of sensitive and proprietary data within a business or organization. It includes measures and policies that ensure the confidentiality of business information, preventing unauthorized access, use, or disclosure.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Customs Privacy Data Policy Catalogue ABB is a comprehensive collection of elements that pertain to the confidentiality of business information. This includes, but is not limited to, trade secrets, financial data, client lists, and marketing strategies. The catalogue emphasizes the importance of implementing appropriate security measures, access controls, non-disclosure agreements, and policies to maintain the confidentiality of business information. The aim is to prevent unauthorized access, use, or disclosure of such information, which could compromise the competitive advantage, reputation, or legal standing of the business.
Example: An example of an element in the Customs Privacy Data Policy Catalogue ABB is 'Confidentiality of Business Information'. This element refers to the protection of sensitive and proprietary data belonging to a business or organization. It involves ensuring that confidential information remains secure and is accessible only to authorized individuals within the organization. Confidentiality safeguards aim to prevent unauthorized access, use, or disclosure of such information.

element.name: Legislation on Structural Interoperability (EBI)
element.documentation:
Definition: Legislation on Structural Interoperability (EBI) ABB is a grouping that covers key regulations issued by the European Union to establish a framework for electronic identification, trust services, and cybersecurity in the internal market. It includes regulations that aim to enhance the security and reliability of electronic transactions, promote the use of electronic identification, facilitate the digital single market, and strengthen the resilience of the EU's digital infrastructure.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Legislation on Structural Interoperability (EBI) ABB includes two key regulations. The first, Regulation 2014910, also known as eIDAS, provides a legal framework for electronic signatures, seals, time stamps, documents, and registered delivery services, ensuring their legal validity and cross-border recognition within the EU. The second, Regulation 2018389, establishes a framework for cooperation and information exchange in the field of cybersecurity, setting out rules for sharing information on cyber threats and incidents, coordinating response measures, and establishing a European Cybersecurity Certification Framework.
Example: An example of the application of the Legislation on Structural Interoperability (EBI) ABB is the use of electronic signatures in cross-border transactions within the EU. Under Regulation 2014910 (eIDAS), these signatures are legally valid and recognized across member states, facilitating electronic transactions and promoting the digital single market. Another example is the sharing of information on cyber threats and incidents between member states under Regulation 2018389, which enhances EU cybersecurity capabilities and strengthens the resilience of its digital infrastructure.

element.name: Business Agnostic High Value Dataset Solutions
element.documentation:
Definition: Business Agnostic High Value Dataset Solutions (BAHVDS) is a grouping that covers a wide range of high-value datasets that are not specific to any particular business sector. These datasets include Geospatial, Business-related data, Metereology, Mobility, Statistics, and Earth Observation Data. Each of these datasets comprises different types of data, such as INSPIRE themes, reference parcels, agricultural parcels, company information, records, financial statements, weather data, river information services data, statistical data, and environmental information.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The BAHVDS is a comprehensive catalogue of high-value datasets that are applicable across various business sectors. The Geospatial High Value Dataset includes INSPIRE themes, reference parcels, and agricultural parcels. The Business-related data High Value Dataset includes basic company information, records, and financial statements. The Metereology High Value Dataset includes observation measurement data (weather stations), climate data, weather warnings, radar data, NWP model data. The Mobility High Value Dataset includes INSPIRE themes and River Information Services data. The Statistics High Value Dataset includes statistical data on select legal acts. The Earth Observation Data High Value Dataset includes INSPIRE themes, environmental information according to the environmental information directive, and datasets related to select legal acts.
Example: Examples of application of these datasets could be in various sectors such as agriculture, where the Geospatial High Value Dataset could be used for land management and planning. The Business-related data High Value Dataset could be used by financial institutions for risk assessment and credit scoring. The Metereology High Value Dataset could be used by weather forecasting agencies for accurate weather prediction. The Mobility High Value Dataset could be used for transportation planning and management. The Statistics High Value Dataset could be used by government agencies for policy making. The Earth Observation Data High Value Dataset could be used for environmental monitoring and conservation.

element.name: Scalability Requirements Catalogue
element.documentation:
Definition: Scalability Requirements Catalogue ABB is a grouping that covers a range of non-functional IT requirements that are critical for ensuring the scalability, performance, and efficiency of a system or application. It includes elements such as Traffic Pattern, Elasticity, and Latency, each of which plays a key role in determining how well a system can handle user traffic and respond to changes in demand.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Scalability Requirements Catalogue ABB is a comprehensive collection of non-functional requirements that are essential for the design and operation of scalable IT systems. The 'Traffic Pattern' element refers to the expected volume and frequency of user traffic, which helps in planning the necessary infrastructure and resources. 'Elasticity' refers to the system's ability to scale up or down based on demand, ensuring optimal performance and cost-efficiency. 'Latency', on the other hand, refers to the time delay between a request and response, which is a crucial factor in the overall user experience. By considering these elements, IT professionals can design systems that are robust, scalable, and efficient, meeting the needs of users while optimizing resource utilization.
Example: For instance, a video streaming service needs to consider all these elements in their system design. The 'Traffic Pattern' would help them prepare for peak viewing times and ensure the system can handle the load. 'Elasticity' would allow the service to scale up during popular live events and scale down during off-peak hours, optimizing resource use. Lastly, 'Latency' is critical for providing a smooth viewing experience, as high latency could lead to buffering and lagging issues.

element.name: Business Agnostic Containers Orchestrator Solutions
element.documentation:
Description: Containers Orchestrator Solutions ABB is a Grouping that refers to actual solutions that facilitate the management, scaling, networking, and deployment of containerized applications. These solutions provide an automated framework for running and coordinating containers within and across different environments.
Additional information: Container orchestrator solutions are essential in modern application development and deployment, especially in cloud-based and microservices architectures. They handle the lifecycle of containers, from provisioning and deployment to networking, scaling, and load balancing. They also ensure the health and availability of containers, restarting failed containers, and replacing and rescheduling containers when nodes die. Some of the most popular container orchestrator solutions include Kubernetes, Docker Swarm, and Apache Mesos.
Example: 1. Kubernetes is a widely used container orchestrator solution that automates the deployment, scaling, and management of containerized applications. 2. Docker Swarm is another example, which allows for the management of a cluster of Docker nodes as a single virtual system. 3. Apache Mesos is a project that manages computer clusters and provides efficient resource isolation and sharing across distributed applications or frameworks.
Publisher: EIRA Team Research

property.value: 1. Kubernetes is a widely used container orchestrator solution that automates the deployment, scaling, and management of containerized applications. 2. Docker Swarm is another example, which allows for the management of a cluster of Docker nodes as a single virtual system. 3. Apache Mesos is a project that manages computer clusters and provides efficient resource isolation and sharing across distributed applications or frameworks.

Container orchestrator solutions are essential in modern application development and deployment, especially in cloud-based and microservices architectures. They handle the lifecycle of containers, from provisioning and deployment to networking, scaling, and load balancing. They also ensure the health and availability of containers, restarting failed containers, and replacing and rescheduling containers when nodes die. Some of the most popular container orchestrator solutions include Kubernetes, Docker Swarm, and Apache Mesos.

Containers Orchestrator Solutions ABB is a Grouping that refers to actual solutions that facilitate the management, scaling, networking, and deployment of containerized applications. These solutions provide an automated framework for running and coordinating containers within and across different environments.

element.name: Business Agnostic Blockchain Solutions
element.documentation:
Description: Blockchain Solutions ABB is a grouping that refers to actual solutions that facilitate the use of blockchain technology in various industries. These solutions are designed to leverage the unique features of blockchain such as decentralization, transparency, security, and immutability to improve business processes, enhance trust, and reduce operational costs.
Additional information: Blockchain Solutions ABB encompasses a wide range of services and applications that utilize blockchain technology. These solutions can be tailored to meet the specific needs of different industries, including finance, supply chain, healthcare, and more. They can be used to create secure and transparent transaction networks, track and verify the authenticity of goods, manage digital identities, and much more. Blockchain Solutions ABB can also include consulting services to help businesses understand and implement blockchain technology effectively.
Example: Examples of Blockchain Solutions ABB include blockchain-based supply chain management systems that provide end-to-end visibility and traceability of goods, blockchain-based financial systems that enable secure and transparent transactions, and blockchain-based healthcare systems that ensure the security and privacy of patient data. Another example is the use of blockchain for energy trading, where ABB has developed a solution that allows for peer-to-peer energy transactions, improving efficiency and reducing costs.

element.name: Legislation on Structural Interoperability (NNBI)
element.documentation:
Definition: Legislation on Structural Interoperability (NNBI) ABB is a grouping that covers the legal and regulatory framework related to the structural interoperability of systems, networks, and services. It includes laws, regulations, directives, and other legal instruments that govern the design, implementation, and operation of interoperable systems and services.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The NNBI ABB is a comprehensive catalogue of legal and regulatory instruments that are relevant to structural interoperability. It provides a structured and systematic approach to understanding and navigating the complex legal landscape of interoperability. The catalogue includes a wide range of elements, each with a specific name and description. These elements represent different aspects of the legal and regulatory framework for interoperability, including specific laws and regulations, overarching legal principles, regulatory authorities and their roles, compliance requirements, and enforcement mechanisms. The NNBI ABB is an essential resource for policymakers, regulators, industry professionals, and other stakeholders involved in the design, implementation, and operation of interoperable systems and services.
Example: Examples of application of the Legislation on Structural Interoperability (NNBI) ABB could include the development of a new digital communication network that needs to comply with specific interoperability standards, or a public administration implementing a new e-government service that needs to be compatible with existing systems and services. In these cases, the NNBI ABB would provide a comprehensive overview of the relevant legal and regulatory requirements, helping to ensure compliance and avoid potential legal and regulatory pitfalls.
LOST view: LV-Architecture Principles

element.name: Solution Architect Concerns
element.documentation:
Definition: Solution Architect Concerns ABB is a Grouping that covers the processes a solution architect should follow, and the relation/influence of process related with other roles' processes, to read/assess/understand an eGovERA model. It includes the journeys of various roles such as Public Policy Officer, Governance Analyst, Information Architect, Software Architect, and Infrastructure Architect.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Solution Architect Concerns ABB is a comprehensive catalogue that outlines the key concerns and processes that a solution architect should consider when working with an eGovERA model. It includes the journeys of various roles, providing a detailed roadmap for each. The Public Policy Officer Journey, for instance, outlines the steps a public policy officer would take in the context of the eGovERA model. Similarly, the Governance Analyst Journey, Information Architect Journey, Software Architect Journey, and Infrastructure Architect Journey provide a step-by-step guide for these roles. Each journey is designed to help the solution architect understand the processes, responsibilities, and concerns of these roles, thereby enabling them to better assess and understand the eGovERA model.
Example: For instance, the 'Public Policy Officer Journey' might include steps like 'Identify Policy Needs', 'Develop Policy Proposal', 'Implement Policy', and 'Evaluate Policy Impact'. Similarly, the 'Software Architect Journey' might include steps like 'Define Software Requirements', 'Design Software Architecture', 'Implement Software', and 'Test and Validate Software'. By understanding these journeys, a solution architect can better understand how each role interacts with the eGovERA model and can therefore design more effective solutions.
LOST view: [A] How to read the model

element.name: Business Agnostic Organisational Governance Frameworks Catalogue
element.documentation:
Definition: Organisational Governance Frameworks Catalogue ABB is a grouping that covers a set of business objects that enable the protection, confidentiality, and interoperability of data, information, and knowledge assets and the organizational resources handling them. It includes the Security Framework, Privacy Framework, and Interoperability Framework.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Organisational Governance Frameworks Catalogue ABB is a comprehensive collection of frameworks that are designed to guide organizations in managing and protecting their data and information assets. The Security Framework focuses on the protection of these assets and the resources handling them. The Privacy Framework, on the other hand, emphasizes the confidentiality aspects of these assets and resources. Lastly, the Interoperability Framework is designed to enable organizations to collaborate effectively towards the joint delivery of public services. It does this by specifying a set of common elements such as vocabulary, concepts, principles, guidelines, and recommendations.
Example: An example of the application of the Organisational Governance Frameworks Catalogue ABB could be a public service organization that needs to ensure the security and privacy of its data while also needing to collaborate with other organizations. The Security Framework would guide the organization in protecting its data and resources. The Privacy Framework would help ensure the confidentiality of the data. The Interoperability Framework would provide the necessary guidelines and recommendations for effective collaboration with other organizations.
LOST view: OV-Governance Architecture Principles

element.name: Identification and Access Enablers
element.documentation:
Definition: Identification and Access Enablers ABB is a Grouping that refers to components to enable the secure identification and authentication of users, systems and services into a platform.
Source: World Bank
Source reference: https://id4d.worldbank.org/guide/enablers
Example: The following implementation is an example on how this specific Architecture Building Block (ABB) can be instantiated as a Solution Building Block (SBB): EU Login - EU Login is the European Commission's user authentication service. It allows authorised users to access a wide range of Commission web services. EU Login is the entry gate to sign in to different European Commission services and/or other systems. EU Login verifies your identity and allows recovering your personal settings, history and access rights in a secure way. You can sign in using social media accounts or the EU Login account. EU Login supports a variety of verification methods: • Password; • ECAS Mobile App PIN code; • ECAS Mobile App QR code; • On mobile authentication; • Mobile phone + SMS; • Token and Token CRAM. https://webgate.ec.europa.eu/cas/about.html
Interoperability Dimension: Structural IoP
LOST view: Technical view - application
Interoperability Saliency: The Identification and Access Enablers Grouping ABB is salient for interoperability because it is composed of the different tools, mechanisms and platforms that can ensure the access rights, and the confidentiality of data. In general terms, identification and authentication are relevant aspects that can enable trustworthy data exchanges or harm data in interoperable digital services.

element.name: Legislation on Behavioural Interoperability (ENBI)
element.documentation:
Definition: Legislation on Behavioural Interoperability (ENBI) ABB is a grouping that covers the legal and regulatory aspects related to the interaction between different systems and software applications. It includes the rules, standards, and protocols that govern how these systems communicate and exchange data, ensuring that they can work together effectively and efficiently.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The ENBI ABB does not contain any specific elements as indicated by the provided JSON. However, in a broader context, it would typically encompass elements such as data exchange protocols, communication standards, security regulations, privacy laws, and other legal requirements related to interoperability. These elements are crucial in ensuring that different systems can interact with each other without any issues, while also maintaining the security and privacy of the data being exchanged. The ENBI ABB would be applicable in various fields, including IT, telecommunications, healthcare, and more.
Example: An example of application could be in the healthcare sector, where different systems need to exchange patient data. The ENBI ABB would cover the legal requirements for this data exchange, such as the need for patient consent, the standards for data encryption, and the protocols for data transmission. This ensures that the systems can interact effectively, while also protecting the privacy and security of the patient data.

element.name: Business Agnostic Observability and Monitoring Solutions
element.documentation:
Description: Observability and Monitoring Solutions ABB is a grouping that refers to actual solutions that facilitate the collection, processing, storage, indexing, and visualization of data from various sources, particularly in the context of microservices and other applications. This grouping includes tools for centralized logging and log analysis, as well as metrics instrumentation for monitoring system performance.
Additional information: The Observability and Monitoring Solutions ABB grouping includes tools such as the ELK Stack and Micrometer. The ELK Stack is a collection of three open-source tools: Elasticsearch, Logstash, and Kibana. Elasticsearch is a distributed search and analytics engine that stores and indexes data, providing fast and scalable search capabilities. Logstash is a data processing pipeline that ingests, transforms, and sends data to Elasticsearch. Kibana is a data visualization and exploration platform that allows users to interact with the data stored in Elasticsearch, creating real-time dashboards, charts, and graphs. On the other hand, Micrometer is an open-source dimensional metrics instrumentation library for microservices and other applications. It provides a simple and consistent API for collecting application metrics, such as response times, error rates, and throughput, from various monitoring systems. Micrometer supports a wide range of monitoring systems, including Prometheus, Graphite, InfluxDB, and more, allowing developers to choose the system that best fits their needs.
Example: For example, a company could use the ELK Stack to centralize logging from various sources, making it easier to analyze and visualize data in real time. They could also use Micrometer to collect metrics from their microservices, helping them monitor system performance and identify potential issues before they become major problems.

element.name: Customs Legislation on Governance Interoperability (ENBI)
element.documentation:
Definition: Customs Legislation on Governance Interoperability (ENBI) ABB is a Grouping that covers the set of rules, regulations, and standards that facilitate the exchange and mutual understanding of information between different customs governance systems. It aims to ensure seamless and efficient communication and cooperation between various customs authorities and stakeholders, thereby enhancing the effectiveness and efficiency of customs operations.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: ENBI is crucial in the modern global trade environment where customs operations involve multiple jurisdictions and numerous stakeholders. It covers aspects such as data exchange standards, communication protocols, security measures, and legal frameworks that enable interoperability. It aims to ensure that different customs systems can work together seamlessly, reducing delays and costs, and enhancing the security and efficiency of international trade. The elements contained within ENBI can vary widely, including technical standards, legal agreements, operational procedures, and more.
Example: An example of ENBI application could be the implementation of a common data exchange standard across different customs systems, allowing them to share and understand the same information. Another example could be the establishment of a legal framework that enables the mutual recognition of customs controls and procedures, reducing the need for duplicate checks and speeding up the customs process.

element.name: Customs Base Registry
element.documentation:
Definition: Customs Base Registry ABB is a Grouping that covers a range of systems and identifiers used in the regulation and facilitation of international trade. These elements include the Registered Exporter system (REX), Economic Operators Registration and Identification number (EORI), Import Control System (ICS), Integrated Tariff of the European Union (TARIC), VAT Information Exchange System (VIES), and the Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) status.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Customs Base Registry is a comprehensive catalogue of systems and identifiers used in international trade. The REX system allows for self-certification of goods' origin by registered exporters. The EORI system assigns unique identification numbers to economic operators involved in customs activities within the EU. The ICS is an EU system designed to enhance customs control over goods entering the EU. TARIC is an integrated tariff database that contains information on customs tariffs, import and export formalities, and applicable measures. VIES is a system that enables businesses to verify the validity of VAT numbers of their trading partners within the EU. AEO is a status granted to businesses by customs administrations in the EU and many other countries worldwide, recognizing businesses that meet certain criteria and demonstrate compliance with customs regulations and security standards.
Example: For example, a business exporting goods from the EU would need to register in the REX system to self-certify the origin of their goods.
