element.name: Customs Legislation on Structural Interoperability (NBI)
element.documentation:
Definition: Customs Legislation on Structural Interoperability (NBI) ABB is a grouping that covers the legal and regulatory framework that governs the exchange of data and information between different systems, platforms, and applications within the customs environment. This includes laws, regulations, and guidelines that ensure seamless integration and interaction between different systems for efficient customs operations.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Customs Legislation on Structural Interoperability (NBI) ABB is crucial in facilitating international trade. It ensures that different systems can effectively communicate and exchange data, thereby enhancing efficiency, reducing errors, and promoting transparency in customs operations. This legislation covers various aspects including data formats, communication protocols, security standards, and data integrity checks among others. It is applicable to all stakeholders involved in customs operations including customs authorities, traders, freight forwarders, and other government agencies.
Example: An example of application of the Customs Legislation on Structural Interoperability (NBI) ABB is in the implementation of a Single Window system. This system allows traders to submit all required documents and data for customs clearance through a single entry point. The legislation ensures that the Single Window system can seamlessly interact with other systems such as the traders' systems, freight forwarders' systems, and other government agencies' systems to facilitate efficient data exchange and processing.

element.name: Legislation on Structural Interoperability (NBI)
element.documentation:
Definition: Legislation on Structural Interoperability (NBI) is a grouping that covers national schemas on eIdentification, cybersecurity, eDelivery, and access to base registries. These schemas provide a framework for the implementation of digital services and security measures in a national context.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Legislation on Structural Interoperability (NBI) is a comprehensive catalogue of information entities that provide the legal and structural framework for the implementation of digital services and security measures at a national level. It includes the National Schema on eIdentification, which outlines the standards and protocols for digital identification processes. The National Schema on Cybersecurity provides the guidelines for implementing cybersecurity measures and protocols. The National Schema on eDelivery outlines the framework for electronic delivery of services, while the National Schema on the access to Base Registries provides the guidelines for accessing base registries in a digital environment.
Example: For example, a country implementing a new digital identification system would refer to the National Schema on eIdentification within the Legislation on Structural Interoperability (NBI) to ensure they are following the correct standards and protocols. Similarly, if a country is looking to enhance its cybersecurity measures, it would refer to the National Schema on Cybersecurity for guidance.

element.name: Business Agnostic Technical Governance Catalogue
element.documentation:
Definition: Business Agnostic Technical Governance Catalogue (ABB) is a grouping that covers the various forms of blockchain governance. These forms include Hybrid Blockchain Governance, Public Blockchain Governance (permissionless), Private Blockchain Governance (permissioned), and Blockchain Governance in general.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Business Agnostic Technical Governance Catalogue is a comprehensive collection of different types of blockchain governance. It includes Hybrid Blockchain Governance, which combines aspects of both public and private blockchains. Public Blockchain Governance (permissionless) is a type of blockchain where anyone can join and participate in the decision-making process. Private Blockchain Governance (permissioned) is a type of blockchain where only selected entities are allowed to participate in the consensus process. Lastly, Blockchain Governance in general refers to the system of rules and procedures that regulate the operation and maintenance of a blockchain network.
Example: An example of Hybrid Blockchain Governance is the Ripple network, which combines aspects of both public and private blockchains. It allows certain nodes to participate in the consensus process, while also allowing anyone to hold and transfer its native cryptocurrency, XRP. Bitcoin is a prime example of Public Blockchain Governance (permissionless). Anyone can join the network, participate in the mining process, and have a say in the decision-making process. An example of Private Blockchain Governance (permissioned) is the Hyperledger Fabric, where only selected entities are allowed to participate in the consensus process. Ethereum is an example of Blockchain Governance. It has a system of rules and procedures that regulate the operation and maintenance of the network, including the process of decision-making and the implementation of changes to the protocol.
LOST view: TVI-Governance Architecture Principles

element.name: Customs Data Exchange Solutions
element.documentation:
Definition: Customs Data Exchange Solutions ABB is a Grouping that covers a range of solutions designed to facilitate the exchange of customs data between different entities. The main objective of these solutions is to streamline the processes of data management and make all relevant information readily available. The European Commission has designed a centralised system for this purpose, known as the INF SP System.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: Customs Data Exchange Solutions ABB includes the 'Central system for the standardised exchange of information', also known as the INF SP System. This system is designed to standardise the exchange of information and streamline the processes of data management. It aims to make all INF data available in a centralised manner, thereby improving efficiency and reducing the potential for errors. The system is designed by the European Commission and is part of their efforts to improve customs procedures across the EU.
Example: An example of the application of the Customs Data Exchange Solutions ABB is the use of the INF SP System by customs authorities across the EU. This system allows for the standardised exchange of information, making it easier for these authorities to access and manage the data they need. This can help to speed up customs procedures and improve the accuracy of the data being used.

element.name: Digital Public Service Strategy (Public Policy Cycle) Principle Catalogue
element.documentation:
Definition: Digital Public Service Strategy (Public Policy Cycle) Principle Catalogue ABB is a grouping that covers a range of principles and strategies related to the implementation and management of digital public services. These principles include accessibility, accountability, best fit public service implementation orientation, care from cradle to grave, data sovereignty, deployment fit (Cloud-first approach), digital first, digital partnership, digital sovereignty and autonomy, evidence-based public policy, social participation, transparency of internal information systems, and transparency of the administrative environment.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The catalogue is a comprehensive collection of principles and strategies that guide the implementation, management, and evolution of digital public services. 'Accessibility' ensures services are available to all citizens, 'Accountability' ensures responsible use of resources and power, 'Best fit Public Service Implementation Orientation' guides the implementation process, 'Care from cradle to grave' ensures lifelong support for citizens, 'Data Sovereignty' ensures citizens' data rights, 'Deployment fit (Cloud-first approach)' guides the deployment of services, 'Digital First' prioritizes digital solutions, 'Digital Partnership' encourages collaboration, 'Digital sovereignty and autonomy' ensures digital independence, 'Evidence based Public Policy' ensures policies are based on factual data, 'Social participation' encourages citizen involvement, 'Transparency of internal information systems' ensures openness about system operations, and 'Transparency of the administrative environment' ensures openness about administrative processes.
Example: An example of 'Accessibility' could be a government website that is designed to be user-friendly for all citizens, including those with disabilities. An example of 'Accountability' could be a public service agency that regularly publishes reports on its spending and activities. An example of 'Best fit Public Service Implementation Orientation' could be a government agency that carefully selects the most suitable software for its needs, rather than simply choosing the most popular or cheapest option. An example of 'Care from cradle to grave' could be a government health service that provides care for citizens from birth to old age.
LOST view: Architecture Principles view
Identifier: http://data.europa.eu/dr8/egovera/DigitalPublicServiceStrategyPrincipleCatalogueGrouping
ABB name: egovera:DigitalPublicServiceStrategyPrincipleCatalogueGrouping
EIRA concept: eira:ArchitectureBuildingBlock

element.name: Business Agnostic Controlled Vocabulary Solutions
element.documentation:
Definition: Business Agnostic Controlled Vocabulary Solutions (BACVS) is a grouping that covers a range of vocabularies and models designed to standardize and simplify data and information exchange across various domains. These vocabularies are context-neutral, reusable, and extensible, making them applicable across different business environments and sectors.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The BACVS includes elements such as the eGovernment Core Vocabularies, Core Assessment Vocabulary, Core Standards and Specifications Vocabulary, W3C Profiles Vocabulary, and EuroVoc. These vocabularies are designed to capture the fundamental characteristics of a data entity, define assessments of assets, facilitate information exchange related to software standards and specifications, allow machine-readable descriptions of profiles of specifications for information resources, and provide a multilingual and multidisciplinary thesaurus for the EU, respectively. They are all domain-agnostic, meaning they can be applied across various business sectors and environments.
Example: These vocabularies can be used by government agencies to standardize data exchange and communication, ensuring consistency and interoperability across different systems and platforms.
This vocabulary can be used by businesses to assess various types of assets based on specific criteria, ensuring a standardized and comprehensive assessment process.
Software developers can use this vocabulary to facilitate information exchange related to software standards and specifications, promoting interoperability and standardization.
This vocabulary can be used by organizations to create machine-readable descriptions of profiles of specifications for information resources, promoting transparency and accessibility.
EU institutions can use EuroVoc to describe the content of documents in EUR-Lex, promoting consistency and clarity in document classification and retrieval.

element.name: Digital Public Service Design Principle Catalogue
element.documentation:
Definition: Digital Public Service Design Principle Catalogue ABB is a grouping that covers a range of principles and guidelines aimed at shaping the design and implementation of digital public services. These principles encompass various aspects including administrative simplification, carbon-dioxide e-footprint impact awareness, code of ethics compliance, data portability, EU legislation compliance, integrated user experience, multilingualism, privacy, proactiveness, service orientation, technology neutrality, and user-centricity among others.
Source: EIRA Team Research
Additional information: The Digital Public Service Design Principle Catalogue ABB is a comprehensive collection of principles that guide the design and delivery of digital public services. These principles are aimed at ensuring that digital services are user-centric, efficient, ethical, and compliant with relevant legislation. They cover a broad spectrum of considerations from administrative simplification which aims to reduce bureaucratic processes and make public services more accessible, to carbon-dioxide e-footprint impact awareness which encourages the design of digital services that are environmentally friendly. Other principles like data portability and privacy ensure that users' data is handled responsibly and securely. The catalogue also includes principles like multilingualism and integrated user experience which aim to make digital services more inclusive and user-friendly.
Example: An example of application of these principles can be seen in the design of a digital public service like an online tax filing system. The system would need to be designed with user-centricity in mind, ensuring it is easy to use for all citizens. It would also need to comply with EU legislation and a code of ethics, ensuring data is handled securely and responsibly. The system should also be designed with an awareness of its carbon-dioxide e-footprint, aiming to minimise its environmental impact. Furthermore, the principle of administrative simplification would be applied to make the tax filing process as straightforward and efficient as possible.
LOST view: Architecture Principles view

view.name: TVA-Analytics Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVA-Analytics Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - application and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging the Business Agnostic Digital Public Services Catalogue and the Analytics Enablers.
The Business Agnostic Digital Public Services Catalogue is a Diagram Model-group ABB that encompasses the Data Analytics Business Service ABB. This service provides digital public services related to data analytics.
The Analytics Enablers is a Grouping ABB that refers to components and services that serve any current or future Digital Service Infrastructure (DSI) requiring data analysis capabilities. This grouping includes several Application Service ABBs: Big Data Analytics, Data Analytics, Business Intelligence, and Smart Queue Management.
The Big Data Analytics Application Service refers to a software application or platform that leverages advanced analytics techniques to process and analyze large and complex datasets, commonly known as big data. It enables organizations to derive valuable insights, identify patterns, trends, and correlations, and make data-driven decisions. The service typically includes data ingestion, storage, processing, and visualization capabilities, as well as advanced analytics techniques such as machine learning, natural language processing, and predictive modeling.
The Data Analytics ABB is an Application Service that enables the use of procedures to analyze data and extract insights that can be used to improve business decision-making, optimize business processes, and drive innovation.
The Business Intelligence Application Service ABB is another component of the Analytics Enablers, providing business intelligence capabilities.
Lastly, the Smart Queue Management Application Service ABB is part of the Analytics Enablers, providing smart queue management capabilities.
The motivation behind this view is to provide a comprehensive framework that leverages the capabilities of the Business Agnostic Digital Public Services Catalogue and the Analytics Enablers to enhance data analysis capabilities and support data-driven decision-making in the organization.

node.label: Business Agnostic Digital Public Services Catalogue

view.name: TVA-Knowledge Discovery Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVA-Knowledge Discovery Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - application and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging the elements of the JSON provided. The view is primarily composed of two main elements: the 'Business Agnostic Knowledge Discovery Service' and the 'Knowledge Discovery Enablers'.
The 'Business Agnostic Knowledge Discovery Service' is a Diagram Model-group ABB that encapsulates the 'Knowledge Management' Business Service ABB. This service is described as a digital public service that is dedicated to the management of knowledge. However, the JSON does not provide any sub-elements or further details about this service.
The 'Knowledge Discovery Enablers' is a Grouping ABB that refers to components and services that facilitate the process of discovering insights and knowledge from data. This group includes four Application Service ABBs: 'Knowledge Discovery', 'Knowledge Management', 'Knowledge Exchange', and 'Vocabulary Hub'.
The 'Knowledge Discovery' service is described as a highly complex process where a lot of data manipulation tools with different characteristics have to be used together to reach the goal of previously unknown, potentially useful information extraction.
The 'Knowledge Management' service is a software application or service that supports the processes of capturing, organizing, storing, retrieving, and sharing knowledge within an organization. It provides functionalities and tools to facilitate knowledge creation, acquisition, categorization, search, collaboration, and dissemination. This service enables employees or users to access and leverage the organization's knowledge assets effectively, fostering innovation, decision-making, and continuous learning.
The 'Knowledge Exchange' service is not described in detail in the JSON, but it can be inferred that it is related to the exchange or sharing of knowledge.
The 'Vocabulary Hub' service is also not described in detail in the JSON. However, it can be inferred that it is a service related to managing and providing access to a vocabulary or set of terminologies used within the organization or system.
In summary, the TVA-Knowledge Discovery Enablers [Motivation] view provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging various services and components that enable the discovery, management, exchange, and use of knowledge in an organization.

view.name: TVA-Customs Risk Analysis Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVA-Customs Risk Analysis Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - application and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging the capabilities of the 'Customs Risk Management and Analysis Enablers' and 'Customs Digital Public Services'.
The 'Customs Risk Management and Analysis Enablers' is a Grouping ABB that encapsulates the 'Risk analysis' Application Service ABB. This service refers to the systematic assessment and evaluation of potential risks associated with trade transactions and customs operations. It involves leveraging data analytics, algorithms, and risk management methodologies to identify patterns, anomalies, and potential risks in real-time. By analyzing factors such as shipment details, trader profiles, country of origin, and historical data, risk analysis enables customs authorities to prioritize inspections, allocate resources effectively, and mitigate risks related to smuggling, fraud, security threats, and non-compliance. This digital solution service enhances customs efficiency, facilitates secure trade, and supports informed decision-making to ensure effective risk management within the customs domain.
The 'Customs Digital Public Services' is a Diagram Model-group ABB that includes the 'Risk analysis' Business Service ABB. This service is a digital public service that is part of the customs digital public services.
The relationship between these two elements is that the 'Risk analysis' Application Service ABB under 'Customs Risk Management and Analysis Enablers' is the technical enabler for the 'Risk analysis' Business Service ABB under 'Customs Digital Public Services'. This means that the application service provides the necessary technical capabilities and functionalities that enable the business service to deliver its intended value to the users.
The motivation for this arrangement is to ensure that the customs authorities can effectively manage and mitigate risks associated with trade transactions and customs operations by leveraging advanced data analytics and risk management methodologies. This not only enhances customs efficiency and facilitates secure trade but also supports informed decision-making.

view.name: TVA-Customs Data Management Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVA-Customs Data Management Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - application and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging digital technologies to enhance the management and oversight of customs processes. This view is divided into two main elements: "Customs Data Management Enablers" and "Customs Digital Public Services".
The "Customs Data Management Enablers" group comprises two application services: "Preservation of cargo information" and "Laboratories management". The "Preservation of cargo information" service refers to the secure and systematic management of data related to the movement and handling of goods during customs processes. This service involves the digital capture, storage, and retrieval of cargo-related information, such as shipping details, transport documents, customs declarations, and inspection reports. By leveraging digital technologies, including data management systems, document repositories, and secure data transmission protocols, this service ensures the integrity, traceability, and accessibility of critical data throughout the customs clearance process.
The second service, "Laboratories management", refers to the implementation of digital tools and systems to efficiently manage and oversee customs laboratories' operations. This service involves the automation and optimization of laboratory processes, such as sample tracking, test management, result analysis, and quality assurance. By leveraging digital technologies like laboratory information management systems (LIMS), electronic data capture, and data analytics, this service enhances the accuracy, traceability, and efficiency of laboratory testing and analysis within the customs environment.
The "Customs Digital Public Services" group includes two business services: "Preservation of cargo control" and "Laboratories registry management". These services represent the digital public services provided by the customs department to facilitate cargo control and manage laboratories registry. The exact nature and functionality of these services are not detailed in the provided JSON.
In summary, the TVA-Customs Data Management Enablers [Motivation] view presents a framework that leverages digital technologies to enhance customs processes. It highlights the importance of data management and digital tools in ensuring efficient and effective customs operations.

view.name: TVA-Customs Process Streamlining and Efficiency Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVA-Customs Process Streamlining and Efficiency Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - application and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging digital tools and technologies to enhance customs operations and facilitate trade. This view is composed of two main elements: 'Customs Process Streamlining and Efficiency Enablers' and 'Customs Digital Public Services'.
The 'Customs Process Streamlining and Efficiency Enablers' is a Grouping ABB that encompasses three Application Service ABBs: 'Expeditions controls', 'People and skill allocation and distribution', and 'Guarantee'.
'Expeditions controls' refers to the use of digital tools and technologies to enhance the monitoring, tracking, and control of goods throughout the transportation and logistics process. This service involves the implementation of digital systems, such as Electronic Data Interchange (EDI), Global Positioning System (GPS), and Internet of Things (IoT) devices, to enable real-time visibility and management of expeditions.
'People and skill allocation and distribution' refers to the utilization of digital tools and platforms to efficiently allocate, manage, and distribute human resources and skills within the customs organization. This service involves the implementation of digital workforce management systems that enable customs authorities to streamline resource allocation, monitor staff availability, assign tasks, and track skill sets and competencies.
'Guarantee' refers to the electronic management and administration of customs guarantees provided by traders or financial institutions to ensure compliance with customs requirements. This service involves the implementation of digital platforms and systems that enable efficient guarantee management, such as tracking guarantee amounts, issuing and processing electronic guarantee certificates, and automating guarantee-related processes.
The 'Customs Digital Public Services' is a Diagram Model-group ABB that includes the 'Procedure Automation System' as a Business Service ABB. The 'Procedure Automation System' represents a digital public service that automates customs procedures.
The relations between these elements and their motivations are not explicitly defined in the provided JSON. However, it can be inferred that the 'Customs Process Streamlining and Efficiency Enablers' are intended to support the 'Customs Digital Public Services' by providing the necessary digital tools and technologies. The ultimate motivation behind these elements is to enhance customs operations, facilitate trade, and improve the overall efficiency and effectiveness of the customs environment.

view.name: TVA-Customs API Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVA-Customs API Enablers [Motivation] view extends the Technical view - application and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging web services and application interfaces to facilitate customs operations and trade facilitation within the European Union. This view is composed of two main groups: 'Customs Web Services Solutions' and 'Business Agnostic Web Services'.
The 'Customs Web Services Solutions' group consists of several Application Interface SBBs, each representing a specific system or service designed to support customs operations. These systems include CLASS, the EU Customs Trader Portal system, ECICS, TRANSIT, EORI, SAMANCTA, ILIADe, EORI - validation open interface, MRN follow-up, Surveillance System, TARIC, AEO, CDS, COPIS, and EBTI. Each system provides specific functionalities and data to facilitate customs procedures, enhance trade facilitation, and ensure compliance with customs regulations across the European Union.
The 'Business Agnostic Web Services' group consists of several Application Interface ABBs, each representing a generic service that can be utilized across different business contexts. These services include ERP System, eNotification, Financial Management, ePayment, eQualification, eInvoicing, Supply Chain Management, eTendering, eProcurement, eProfessional Qualification, Geo-Localization, and Log Management. Each service provides specific functionalities and data to support various business operations and processes.
The 'Web Service' element, an Application Interface ABB, represents a generic interface that enables interoperability between different applications or systems over the Internet. This element serves as a foundational component for both the 'Customs Web Services Solutions' and 'Business Agnostic Web Services' groups, enabling seamless integration and data exchange between the various systems and services.
The motivation behind this view is to provide a comprehensive framework for leveraging web services and application interfaces to streamline customs operations, enhance trade facilitation, and ensure compliance with customs regulations. By centralizing and standardizing classification information, streamlining customs procedures, and enabling real-time data validation and verification, this view aims to promote secure and efficient cross-border trade within the European Union.

view.name: TVA-Data Exchange Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVA-Data Exchange Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - application and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging the Business Agnostic Data Exchange Business Service and Data Exchange Enablers.
The Business Agnostic Data Exchange Business Service, as depicted in the Diagram Model-group ABB, is a crucial element in this view. It is further detailed by the Data Exchange element, which is a Business Service ABB. The Data Exchange Digital Public Service is designed to facilitate the exchange of data in a business-agnostic manner, meaning it can be used across various business domains.
The Data Exchange Enablers, represented as a Grouping ABB, are essential components that facilitate the exchange of data between systems or applications. This grouping includes two Application Service ABBs: the Once-Only Technical System and the Data Exchange.
The Once-Only Technical System (OOTS) is a cross-sectorial service that enables the sharing of information between public administrations across borders between EU countries. It can be expanded beyond the current scope of life events set out in the Single Digital Gateway Regulation. The OOTS puts into practice the Once-Only Principle, which states that citizens should not be forced to provide information to authorities if another authority already holds that information in electronic format.
The Data Exchange is another Application Service ABB within the Data Exchange Enablers grouping. This service enables the secure exchange of messages, records, forms, and other kinds of data between different individuals, organizations, or systems. This includes data routing, except endpoint discovery.
In summary, the TVA-Data Exchange Enablers [Motivation] view provides a comprehensive framework that leverages the Business Agnostic Data Exchange Business Service and Data Exchange Enablers to facilitate secure and efficient data exchange across different systems, applications, and borders.

node.label: Business Agnostic Data Exchange Business Service

view.name: TVA-Customs Duties and Tariffs Management Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVA-Customs Duties and Tariffs Management Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - application and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging digital technologies and services to enhance the management of customs duties and tariffs.
This view is composed of two main elements: 'Customs Duties and Tariffs Management Enablers' and 'Customs Digital Public Services'.
The 'Customs Duties and Tariffs Management Enablers' is a Grouping ABB that encompasses two Application Service ABBs: 'Tariffs registry management' and 'Duties Calculation and payment'.
'Tariffs registry management' refers to the systematic and automated management of customs tariffs and related information. This service involves the digitalization and centralization of tariff schedules, rates, and updates within a digital registry or database. It enhances transparency, reduces manual errors, improves trade facilitation, and enables efficient tariff determination and assessment within the customs environment.
'Duties Calculation and payment' refers to the automated and accurate determination and processing of customs duties and taxes owed on imported or exported goods. This service leverages digital technologies and algorithms to calculate duties based on factors such as product classification, customs valuation, origin, and applicable trade agreements. It enhances customs efficiency, reduces errors, ensures compliance with customs regulations, and expedites the release of goods, supporting smooth trade operations within the customs environment.
The 'Customs Digital Public Services' is a Diagram Model-group ABB that includes four Business Service ABBs: 'Tariff Registry management', 'Tariff Suspensions', 'Duties calculation and payment', and 'Duties guarantee management'. These services represent the digital public services provided by the customs authorities to facilitate the management of tariffs and duties.
'Tariff Registry management' and 'Duties calculation and payment' Business Service ABBs align with their corresponding Application Service ABBs in the 'Customs Duties and Tariffs Management Enablers' group, indicating that these digital public services are enabled by the underlying application services.
'Tariff Suspensions' and 'Duties guarantee management' represent additional digital public services provided by the customs authorities to manage tariff suspensions and duties guarantees respectively.
Overall, the TVA-Customs Duties and Tariffs Management Enablers [Motivation] view provides a holistic perspective on the digital enablers and services that support efficient and effective management of customs duties and tariffs.

view.name: TVA-Observability and Monitoring Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVA-Observability and Monitoring Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - application and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging the elements of 'Observability and Monitoring Enablers' and 'Business Agnostic Observability and Monitoring Solutions'.
The 'Observability and Monitoring Enablers' is a Grouping ABB (Architecture Building Block) that encapsulates two key elements: 'Observability' and 'Monitoring'. Both of these elements are Application Service ABBs, which are essential services in the architecture. The 'Observability' service is responsible for making the system's internal states externally visible for diagnostic purposes. On the other hand, the 'Monitoring' service is responsible for overseeing the system's operation to ensure it is functioning as expected.
The 'Business Agnostic Observability and Monitoring Solutions' is a Grouping SBB (Solution Building Block) that encompasses two application services: 'ELK Stack' and 'Micrometer'. These are specific solutions that are used to implement the observability and monitoring functionality in a business-agnostic manner. The 'ELK Stack' is an Application Service SBB that provides a powerful platform for searching, analyzing, and visualizing data in real time. The 'Micrometer' is another Application Service SBB that provides a simple facade over the instrumentation clients for the most popular monitoring systems, allowing for dimensional-style metrics collection.
The relationship between these elements is that the 'Observability and Monitoring Enablers' provide the overarching services that are necessary for system diagnostics and operation oversight. These services are then implemented using the specific solutions provided by the 'Business Agnostic Observability and Monitoring Solutions' group. This structure allows for a flexible and adaptable approach to system observability and monitoring, as different solutions can be used depending on the specific needs of the business. The motivation behind this structure is to ensure that the system is always functioning optimally and any issues can be quickly identified and addressed.

view.name: TVA-Digital Workplace Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVA-Digital Workplace Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - application and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging the elements of the Business Agnostic Digital Workplace Business Services and Digital Workplace Enablers.
The Business Agnostic Digital Workplace Business Services is a Diagram Model-group ABB. It is designed to be universally applicable across various business domains. Within this model group, there is a Business Service ABB named Digital Collaboration. This service is described as a Digital Collaboration Digital Public Service, indicating its role in facilitating digital interaction and cooperation in the public sector.
On the other hand, the Digital Workplace Enablers is a Grouping ABB. This grouping refers to components or services that enable the collaboration of work aspects while ensuring security and privacy. Within this grouping, there is an Application Service ABB also named Digital Collaboration. This service, while sharing the same name as the one in the Business Agnostic Digital Workplace Business Services, is distinct in its function and application.
The relationship between these elements is that they are all part of the overarching TVA-Digital Workplace Enablers [Motivation] view. They are interconnected in their shared goal of enabling digital collaboration in the workplace, albeit through different means and in different contexts. The motivation behind these elements and their relationships is to create a comprehensive framework that leverages digital technologies to enhance collaboration and productivity in the workplace, while also ensuring the security and privacy of all involved.

node.label: Business Agnostic Digital Workplace Business Services

view.name: TVA-Customs Data Exchange Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVA-Customs Data Exchange Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - application and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging digital tools and components that facilitate the exchange of data between systems or applications. This view is primarily composed of two main elements: 'Data Exchange Enablers' and 'Customs Data Exchange Solutions'.
The 'Data Exchange Enablers' is a Grouping ABB that refers to tools or components that facilitate the exchange of data between systems or applications. Within this grouping, there are two key elements: 'Data Exchange' as an Application Component ABB and 'Data Exchange' as an Application Service ABB. The 'Data Exchange' Application Component ABB enables the implementation of the procedure to transfer data between different individuals, organizations, or systems. On the other hand, the 'Data Exchange' Application Service ABB enables the secure exchange of messages, records, forms, and other kinds of data between different individuals, organizations, or systems. This includes data routing, except endpoint discovery.
The second main element is the 'Customs Data Exchange Solutions', another Grouping ABB. This grouping contains a key element named 'Central system for the standardized exchange of information', which is an Application Service SBB. The main objective of this system is to make all INF data available and to streamline the processes of INF data management. For this purpose, the European Commission has designed an EU centralized INF SP System.
Additionally, there is an 'Once-Only Technical System', an Application Service ABB, which enables the sharing of information between public administrations across borders between EU countries. It is cross-sectorial and can be expanded beyond the current scope of life events set out in the Single Digital Gateway Regulation. It puts into practice the Once-Only Principle, which states that citizens should not be forced to provide information to authorities if another authority already holds that information in electronic format.
In summary, the TVA-Customs Data Exchange Enablers [Motivation] view provides a detailed framework for data exchange enablers and customs data exchange solutions, highlighting the importance of efficient and secure data exchange between different entities and systems.

view.name: TVA-API Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVA-API Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - application and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging Business Agnostic API Business Services and API Enablers.
The Business Agnostic API Business Services is a Diagram Model-group ABB that includes several Business Service ABBs, namely Log Management, eTendering, eNotification, ePayment, eQualification, and eInvoicing. These services are digital public services that cater to various business needs.
Log Management is a service that deals with the management of digital logs. eTendering is a service that handles digital tendering processes. eNotification is a service that manages digital notifications. ePayment is a service that facilitates digital payments. eQualification is a service that deals with digital qualification processes. eInvoicing is a service that handles digital invoicing.
The API Enablers is a Grouping ABB that refers to components and frameworks that support the implementation and cataloguing of (open) software interfaces. This includes several Application Interface ABBs, namely Web Service, ePayment, eInvoicing, eTendering, eProfessional Qualification, eQualification, eNotification, and Log Management.
Web Service is an Application Interface that enables interoperability between different applications or systems over the Internet. ePayment is an Application Interface that refers to a digital payment solution that enables secure and convenient electronic transactions between buyers and sellers. eInvoicing is an Application Interface that enables the electronic creation, exchange, and processing of invoices between businesses or organizations. eTendering is an Application Interface that provides access to specific functionalities related to tendering processes through web-based APIs. eProfessional Qualification is an Application Interface that enables the management, verification, and processing of professional qualification-related information and services over the internet. eQualification is an Application Interface that enables the management and processing of qualifications and certifications in an electronic format. eNotification is an Application Interface that enables the electronic delivery of notifications, alerts, and messages to individuals or organizations. Log Management is an Application Interface that facilitates the collection, storage, analysis, and monitoring of log data generated by web applications, servers, and other web-based systems.
The motivation behind this view is to provide a comprehensive framework that leverages these services and interfaces to enhance business processes, improve interoperability between different systems, and facilitate secure and efficient digital transactions.

view.name: TVA-Identification and Access Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVA-Identification and Access Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - application and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging the secure identification and authentication of users, systems, and services into a platform. This view is composed of three main elements: Identification and Access Enablers, Business Agnostic Identity Management Solutions, and Business Agnostic Authentication Solutions.
The Identification and Access Enablers is a Grouping ABB that refers to components enabling the secure identification and authentication of users, systems, and services into a platform. It includes several Application Service ABBs and Application Component ABBs, such as Authentication, Registration, Identification, Access Management, Identity Management, Authorisation, Accounting, Request Validation, Centralized Identity Management, and Decentralized Identity Management. Each of these components plays a crucial role in the process of identification and access enabling, from the registration of users to the management of their identities and access rights.
The Business Agnostic Identity Management Solutions is a Grouping SBB that includes several Application Service SBBs, such as eIDAS-Node, eIDAS-Proxy-Service, Keycloak, EU Login, WSO2 Identity Server, and Fraunhofer Omejdn Server. These solutions provide a range of identity management services, from the provision of personal identification data to the management of user authentication and authorization.
The Business Agnostic Authentication Solutions is another Grouping SBB that includes several Application Service SBBs, such as EU Login Identification, EU Login Authentication, EU Login Request Validation, and EU Login Registration. These solutions provide a range of authentication services, from user identification to request validation and registration.
The motivation behind this view is to provide a comprehensive framework for the secure identification and authentication of users, systems, and services into a platform. This is achieved through a combination of various components and solutions, each playing a specific role in the process. The ultimate goal is to ensure that only authorized users have access to the platform and its services, thereby enhancing the security and integrity of the platform.

node.label: EUDI WALLET has to be included here as a SBB for the moment. The logic is that if a high-level model is included in the IoP Arch environment, it should be something developed in co-creation mode with the EUDI WALLET initiative or DIGIT Responsible.

view.name: TVA-Data Space Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVA-Data Space Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - application and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging various components and services that support the creation and management of a dataspace. This view is divided into three main elements: Dataspace Enablers, Business Agnostic Digital Public Services Catalogue, and Business Agnostic Dataspace Solutions.
The Dataspace Enablers, a Grouping ABB, refers to components and services that support the creation and management of a dataspace. Within this grouping, there are two Application Service ABBs: Dataspace and Dataspace Connector. The Dataspace is the virtual space that enables the creation of a single market for data by integrating, transforming, and making available such data. The Dataspace Connector enables the easy and trustworthy procedure to share data and work collaboratively with other research institutions.
The Business Agnostic Digital Public Services Catalogue is another Grouping ABB that includes two Business Service ABBs: Data Space and Data Space Participant. These services are part of the digital public service offerings related to the dataspace.
The third element, Business Agnostic Dataspace Solutions, is a Grouping ABB that includes several Application Service SBBs. These are specific solutions for the dataspace, including the Eclipse Dataspace Connector, International Data Space Connector, FIWARE TRUE Connector, Sovity Dataspace Connector, Intel IONOS Orbiter Connector, and Fraunhofer AISEC Trusted Connector. Each of these services provides specific functionalities and capabilities within the dataspace.
The motivation behind this view is to provide a comprehensive overview of the various components, services, and solutions that enable the creation, management, and utilization of a dataspace. This view helps in understanding the technical and business aspects of the dataspace and how they interact with each other. It also helps in identifying potential opportunities for improvement and innovation within the dataspace.

view.name: TVA-Privacy Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVA-Privacy Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - application and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging various elements that facilitate privacy-related functionality within an application or system.
The view consists of three main elements: 'Business Agnostic Privacy Business Service', 'Privacy Enablers', and 'Business Agnostic Privacy Solutions'.
The 'Business Agnostic Privacy Business Service' is a Diagram Model-group ABB that includes a 'Business Service ABB' named 'Anonymisation'. This service refers to a digital public service that provides anonymisation capabilities, which is a crucial aspect of privacy protection.
The 'Privacy Enablers' is a Grouping ABB that refers to components and services that facilitate the implementation of privacy-related functionality within an application or system. It includes several 'Application Service ABBs' such as 'Privacy', 'Anonymisation', 'Consent Management', 'Data Encryption', and 'Privacy Impact Assessments'.
The 'Privacy' service enables the sharing of functionalities such as storing, securing, anonymising, pseudonymising, rectifying, and erasing personal data. The 'Anonymisation' service refers to a software solution that enables the anonymisation of sensitive or personally identifiable information (PII) within datasets. The 'Consent Management' service, 'Data Encryption' service, and 'Privacy Impact Assessments' service are also part of the 'Privacy Enablers' group, each providing specific functionalities related to privacy protection.
The 'Business Agnostic Privacy Solutions' is a Grouping SBB that serves as a catalogue for privacy solutions. It includes an 'Application Service SBB' named 'HashiCorp Vault', which is a specific application service related to privacy protection.
The motivation behind these elements and their relations is to provide a comprehensive framework for implementing privacy-related functionalities in an application or system. This is crucial in today's digital age, where data protection and privacy are of utmost importance.

view.name: TVA-Customs Trade Facilitation and Collaboration Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVA-Customs Trade Facilitation and Collaboration Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - application and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging digital technologies to enhance efficiency, transparency, and collaboration in customs operations and cross-border trade.
The view is divided into two main groups: 'Customs Trade Facilitation and Collaboration Enablers' and 'Customs Digital Public Services'.
The first group, 'Customs Trade Facilitation and Collaboration Enablers', consists of four application services. The first service, 'Trade Facilitation Portal', is an online platform that simplifies trade procedures and promotes efficiency in cross-border trade. The second service, 'Cooperation between Customs laboratories', involves the use of digital platforms to facilitate collaboration and data exchange between customs laboratories. The third service, 'Cooperation between Customs and Postal Operators', involves the use of digital platforms to facilitate collaboration and data sharing between customs authorities and postal operators. The fourth service, 'MS' Customs organization management', involves the use of digital platforms to manage and oversee the operations of customs organizations within a specific country or region.
The second group, 'Customs Digital Public Services', consists of three business services. The first service, 'Customs organizational structure management', is a digital public service for managing the organizational structure of customs. The second service, 'Laboratories registry management', is a digital public service for managing the registry of laboratories. The third service, 'EU Customs Trader Portal', is a digital public service for traders in the EU customs environment.
These services and platforms are designed to enhance the interoperability of customs operations, improve data accuracy and consistency, foster scientific collaboration, promote trade facilitation, ensure compliance with customs regulations, expedite the clearance and delivery of postal shipments, and contribute to secure and efficient cross-border trade. By leveraging digital technologies, these services and platforms aim to provide a comprehensive framework for customs trade facilitation and collaboration.

view.name: TVA-Translation Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVA-Translation Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - application and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging various elements related to translation services and solutions. This view is composed of three main elements: 'Business Agnostic eTranslation Services', 'Translation Enablers', and 'Business Agnostic Translation Solutions'.
The 'Business Agnostic eTranslation Services' is a Diagram Model-group ABB that encapsulates the business services related to eTranslation. It includes the 'eTranslation' Business Service ABB, which represents the digital public service for eTranslation. This service is business-agnostic, meaning it can be applied across various business domains.
The 'Translation Enablers' is a Grouping ABB that refers to tools or components that facilitate the translation of text from one language to another using machine learning techniques. It includes the 'Machine Translation' Application Service ABB, which enables the procedures for automated translation of text, metadata, and concept classes or nomenclatures. This application service is a key enabler for the translation process, leveraging machine learning techniques to automate and streamline the translation tasks.
The 'Business Agnostic Translation Solutions' is a Grouping SBB that represents a catalogue of translation solutions. It includes the 'eTranslation' Application Service SBB, which represents the application service for eTranslation. This service is part of the translation solutions that are business-agnostic, meaning they can be applied across various business domains.
In terms of relations, the 'Business Agnostic eTranslation Services' and 'Business Agnostic Translation Solutions' are related as they both provide business-agnostic services and solutions for translation. The 'Translation Enablers' is related to both as it provides the necessary tools and components that enable the translation services and solutions. The motivation behind these elements is to provide comprehensive and versatile translation services and solutions that can be applied across various business domains, leveraging machine learning techniques to automate and streamline the translation tasks.

view.name: TVA-Orchestration Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVA-Orchestration Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - application and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging various elements that facilitate business agnostic orchestration.
The first element is the "Business Agnostic Orchestration Business Service," which is a Diagram Model-group ABB. This element encapsulates the "Workflow Management" service, a Business Service ABB that provides a digital public service for managing workflows.
The second element is the "Orchestration Enablers," a Grouping ABB that refers to the components and practices supporting the development and deployment of orchestration applications. This group includes three sub-elements: "Orchestration" as an Application Service ABB, "Orchestration" as an Application Component ABB, and "Workflow Management" as an Application Service ABB. The "Orchestration" Application Service ABB enables the definition of the sequence and conditions in which one service invokes other services to realize some useful function. The "Orchestration" Application Component ABB enables the coordination and management of the execution of multiple components or services within an application or system. The "Workflow Management" Application Service ABB, also known as Orchestration Application Service, refers to a software solution or service that enables the design, execution, and coordination of workflows within an organization.
The third element is the "Business Agnostic Orchestration Solutions," a Grouping SBB that serves as a catalogue for orchestration solutions. This group includes two sub-elements: "Apache Airflow" and "Apache Beam," both of which are Application Service SBBs. These services represent specific orchestration solutions that can be utilized in the orchestration process.
The motivation behind this view is to provide a comprehensive understanding of the various elements and their interrelations that enable effective orchestration in a business-agnostic manner. This includes the services, components, and specific solutions that can be leveraged to design, execute, and manage workflows and orchestration processes within an organization.

view.name: TVA-Containerization Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVA-Containerization Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - application and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging various elements that enable containerization. This view is divided into three main groupings: Containerization Enablers, Business Agnostic Containers Orchestrator Solutions, and Business Agnostic Container Solutions.
The first grouping, Containerization Enablers, is an Architectural Building Block (ABB) that includes two Application Service ABBs: Container and Containers Orchestrator. The Container Application Service represents the basic unit of software that packages up code and all its dependencies so the application runs quickly and reliably from one computing environment to another. The Containers Orchestrator Application Service, on the other hand, is responsible for managing the lifecycles of containers, including deployment, scaling, networking, and availability.
The second grouping, Business Agnostic Containers Orchestrator Solutions, is a Solution Building Block (SBB) that includes five Application Service SBBs: Kubernetes, Docker Compose, Docker Swarm, Apache Mesos, and Red Hat OpenShift. These represent various solutions that can be used to manage and orchestrate containers in a business-agnostic manner, meaning they can be used across different business domains and applications.
The third grouping, Business Agnostic Container Solutions, is also an SBB that includes three Application Service SBBs: Docker, Podman, and LXC. These represent different solutions for creating and managing containers that are also business-agnostic.
The relationships between these elements are defined by their grouping. The Container and Containers Orchestrator are part of the Containerization Enablers, which are necessary for the operation of the Business Agnostic Containers Orchestrator Solutions and the Business Agnostic Container Solutions. These solutions, in turn, provide the tools and services necessary to implement and manage containerization in a business environment. The motivation behind this view is to provide a comprehensive overview of the elements and solutions that enable containerization, allowing for a better understanding and implementation of this technology.

view.name: TVA-Messaging Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVA-Messaging Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - application and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging various elements to facilitate effective messaging. This view is composed of two main elements: 'Messaging Enablers' and 'Business Agnostic Messaging Solutions'.
The 'Messaging Enablers' is a Grouping ABB (Architecture Building Block) that encapsulates the elements that enable messaging. Within this grouping, there is an Application Service ABB named 'Message Broker'. The 'Message Broker' is a crucial component that facilitates the exchange of messages between different applications, acting as an intermediary to ensure smooth communication.
On the other hand, 'Business Agnostic Messaging Solutions' is a Grouping SBB (Solution Building Block) that contains a set of Application Service SBBs. These are 'ActiveMQ', 'Apache Kafka', 'Apache Kafka Streams', and 'RabbitMQ'. These services are independent of any specific business context and can be used across various business scenarios.
'ActiveMQ' is an open-source messaging and Integration Patterns server, which can handle communication from more than one client or server. 'Apache Kafka' is a distributed streaming platform that is designed to handle real-time data feeds. 'Apache Kafka Streams' is a client library for building applications and microservices, where the input and output data are stored in Kafka clusters. 'RabbitMQ' is an open-source message broker software that implements the Advanced Message Queuing Protocol (AMQP).
The relationship between these elements is that the 'Message Broker' in the 'Messaging Enablers' grouping facilitates the communication between the different 'Business Agnostic Messaging Solutions'. These solutions, in turn, provide the necessary services to handle various messaging requirements in a business-agnostic manner. The motivation behind this arrangement is to provide a flexible and robust messaging framework that can cater to diverse business needs.

view.name: TVA-Trust Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVA-Trust Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - application and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging various elements that facilitate secure cross-border transactions and interactions.
The view includes three main groups: Business Agnostic Trust Business Services, Business Agnostic Blockchain Business Service, and Trust Enablers.
The Business Agnostic Trust Business Services group includes the eSignature service, which is a digital public service that enables the signing of data in electronic form by a natural person.
The Business Agnostic Blockchain Business Service group includes the Digital Immutability service, which is a digital public service that ensures the integrity, authenticity, and non-repudiation of digitally signed documents.
The Trust Enablers group refers to components and services that facilitate the establishment and maintenance of secure cross-border transactions and interactions. This group includes various application services such as e-Seal Preservation, e-Timestamp Verification and Validation, Registered Electronic Delivery, e-Seal Verification and Validation, e-Signature Creation, e-Signature Preservation, e-Signature Verification and Validation, e-Seal Creation, e-Timestamp Creation, and Trust Service Provisioning.
These services enable various procedures such as extending the trustworthiness of the qualified electronic signature beyond the technological validity period, verifying timestamps used for establishing evidence that a given piece of data existed at a given point in time, transmitting sensitive or confidential documents and messages between parties, verifying documents that are signed electronically, signing data in electronic form by a natural person, and creating, verifying, or validating electronic signatures, time stamps, seals, electronically registered delivery services, and certificates.
The Trust Enablers group also includes the Blockchain Enablers, which refers to components and services that facilitate the development, deployment, and management of ledger technology applications. This includes the Blockchain and Distributed Ledger application services, which enable secure, transparent, and immutable record-keeping and transaction processing shared by all participants in a network.
The view also includes the Business Agnostic Blockchain Solutions group, which includes the Ethereum and European Blockchain Services Infrastructure application services. These services facilitate the development, deployment, and management of blockchain technology applications.
In addition, the view includes various application services such as Digital Certification Timestamp, Digital Certification eSeal, Digital Certification eSignature Service, Digital Europe eSignature DSS open-source library, and Integrity Verification. These services enable various procedures such as verifying timestamps used for establishing evidence that a given piece of data existed at a given point in time, verifying documents that are signed electronically, securely signing electronic documents using digital certificates, and ensuring that information has not been altered in an unauthorized manner since it was created, transmitted, or stored.

view.name: TVA-Data Management Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVA-Data Management Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - application and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging various elements that facilitate effective data management practices and procedures.
The view is composed of three main groups: Business Agnostic Data Management Business Service, Data Management Enablers, and Business Agnostic Data Governance and Data Integration Solutions.
The Business Agnostic Data Management Business Service group includes six Business Service ABBs: Forms Management, Open Data Management, Data Extraction, Transformation and Loading, Content Management, eArchiving, and Contact Management. These services represent the digital public services that are necessary for managing business-agnostic data.
The Data Management Enablers group refers to components and services that support effective data management practices and procedures. This group includes thirteen Application Service ABBs: Content Management, e-Archiving, Archival Information Packages, Forms Management, Data Extraction, Transformation and Loading, Open Data Management, Contact Management, Data Management, Data Governance, Data Policy Engine, Data Catalogue Management, Federated Data Catalogue Management, Data Integration, and Data Integration Plugins Manager. These services enable various procedures related to data management, such as the creation, management, and publishing of digital content, long-term storage of electronic documents, management of standardized packages of digital content, dynamic creation, distribution and analysis of forms and online surveys, extraction, transformation, and loading of data, and the implementation of procedures to manage data effectively.
The Business Agnostic Data Governance Solutions group includes one Application Service SBB, Apache Atlas, which is a data governance application service. The Business Agnostic Data Integration Solutions group includes four Application Service SBBs: Apache Camel, Apache NiFi, Apache Storm, and Talend Open Studio for Data Integration. These services represent specific solutions for data governance and data integration.
The motivation behind this view is to provide a comprehensive framework that supports effective data management practices and procedures. This is achieved by leveraging various services and components that enable the necessary procedures for managing business-agnostic data, as well as specific solutions for data governance and data integration.

node.label: Business Agnostic Data Management Business Service

view.name: TVA-Artificial Intelligence Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVA-Artificial Intelligence Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - application and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging artificial intelligence (AI) in a business context. This view is composed of two main elements: "Business Agnostic Artificial Intelligence Business Service" and "Artificial Intelligence Enablers".
The "Business Agnostic Artificial Intelligence Business Service" is a Diagram Model-group ABB that represents a business service that is independent of any specific business context. It contains a single element, "Business Intelligence", which is a Business Service ABB that provides a digital public service related to business intelligence.
The "Artificial Intelligence Enablers" is a Grouping ABB that refers to components and services that provide the necessary infrastructure and resources for AI developers to build intelligent systems. These systems are capable of performing tasks that typically require human-like intelligence, such as perception, reasoning, learning, and decision-making. This grouping contains four elements: "Artificial Intelligence", "Machine Learning", "Artificial Intelligence Engine", and "Natural-Language Processing (NLP)".
"Artificial Intelligence" is an Application Service ABB that enables procedures to display intelligent behaviour by analysing their environment and taking actions with some degree of autonomy to achieve specific objectives.
"Machine Learning" is an Application Service ABB within the field of AI that enables systems to automatically learn and improve from experience without being explicitly programmed. It involves the development and deployment of algorithms and models that can analyze large volumes of data, identify patterns, and make predictions or decisions based on the learned patterns.
"Artificial Intelligence Engine" is an Application Service ABB that refers to a software component or service that encompasses the core capabilities of an AI system. It provides a set of algorithms, models, and tools that enable the development, deployment, and execution of AI applications. The AI engine acts as the brain behind AI-powered systems, enabling tasks such as data processing, pattern recognition, prediction, decision-making, and learning.
"Natural-Language Processing (NLP)" is an Application Service ABB that deals with the interaction between computers and humans using natural language. The ultimate objective of NLP is to read, decipher, understand, and make sense of the human language in a valuable way.
In summary, the TVA-Artificial Intelligence Enablers [Motivation] view provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging AI in a business context, including the necessary infrastructure, resources, and services to enable the development and deployment of intelligent systems.

node.label: Business Agnostic Artificial Intelligence Business Service

view.name: TVA-Test Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVA-Test Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - application and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging various elements related to testing and conformance. This view includes elements such as Business Agnostic Testing Business Service, Test Enablers, and Business Agnostic Conformance Solutions.
The Business Agnostic Testing Business Service is a Diagram Model-group ABB that encapsulates the Compliance Testing service. This service is a Business Service ABB that is responsible for the Compliance Testing Digital Public Service.
The Test Enablers is a Grouping ABB that refers to the applications and services that support the development and deployment of conformance testing and validation. It includes elements such as Conformance Testing Application Service ABB, Conformance Testing Application Component ABB, and Conformance Test Scenario Business Object ABB. The Conformance Testing Application Service ABB enables the activities and rules to determine whether a tool, platform, or service faithfully meets the requirements of a standard or specification. The Conformance Testing Application Component ABB enables a structural and modular approach for implementing the validation of the application or service to meet the requirements of a standard or specification. The Conformance Test Scenario Business Object ABB specifies a sequence of actions for the execution of a test, also known as a test script or manual test script.
The Business Agnostic Conformance Solutions is a Grouping SBB that includes elements such as the European Interoperability TestBed and the ETSI Signature Conformance Checker. The European Interoperability TestBed is an Application Service SBB offered by the European Commission's DIGIT to facilitate the conformance testing of IT systems. The TestBed is a software system that can be both downloaded and installed locally, but also reused through a shared online installation operated by DIGIT. The ETSI Signature Conformance Checker is another Application Service SBB provided by ETSI Centre for Testing and Interoperability (CTI) that performs numerous checkings to verify the conformity of the ETSI Advanced Electronic Signatures.
These elements and their relationships provide a comprehensive framework for leveraging the development and deployment of conformance testing and validation.

view.name: TVA-Customs Identification and Access Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVA-Customs Identification and Access Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - application and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging various application services and components to facilitate secure identification and access within the customs domain.
The view is divided into three main elements: 'Customs Identification and Access Solutions', 'Identification and Access Enablers', and 'EU Login' services.
The 'Customs Identification and Access Solutions' element is a Grouping ABB that encompasses four Application Service ABBs: 'Central Uniform User Management and Digital Signature System (UUMDS)', 'TAXUD Identity Management Service', 'TAXUD Authorisation Service', and 'TAXUD Accounting Service'. These services provide functionalities such as managing authorisation assignments, managing and securing digital identities, confirming electronic identification, and tracking and recording access to resources, respectively.
The 'Identification and Access Enablers' element is another Grouping ABB that includes a range of Application Service ABBs and Application Component ABBs. These include 'Authentication', 'Registration', 'Identification', 'Access Management' (both as a service and a component), 'Identity management', 'Authorisation', 'Accounting', and 'Request Validation'. These services and components enable secure identification, authentication, registration, access management, and request validation for users, systems, and services.
The 'EU Login' services include 'EU Login Identification', 'EU Login Authentication', 'EU Login Request Validation', and 'EU Login Registration'. These services, classified as Application Component SBB and Application Service SBB, provide a point for user authentication to a wide range of Commission information systems.
The motivation behind this view is to provide a comprehensive framework that enables secure identification and access within the customs domain. This is achieved through the use of various application services and components that manage and secure digital identities, confirm electronic identification, track and record access to resources, and enable secure identification, authentication, registration, access management, and request validation.

view.name: TVA-Customs Compliance and Regulatory Requirements Enablers [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The TVA-Customs Compliance and Regulatory Requirements Enablers [Motivation] view extends Technical view - application and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging digital technologies to streamline and automate customs procedures, ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements.
The view is divided into two main groups: "Customs Compliance and Regulatory Requirements Enablers" and "Customs Digital Public Services".
The first group, "Customs Compliance and Regulatory Requirements Enablers", consists of six Application Service ABBs: "Special procedure", "Export procedure", "Transit procedure", "Import procedure", "Authorised Economic Operator accreditation", and "Compliance requirements checks". These services represent the implementation of digital platforms and systems designed to automate and streamline various customs procedures, ranging from special procedures that deviate from standard import/export processes to the management of compliance requirements checks.
For example, the "Export procedure" and "Import procedure" services enable traders to electronically submit export and import declarations, relevant documentation, and trade data through a centralized online platform. These digital solutions automate customs processes such as document verification, risk assessment, and export or import clearance, facilitating electronic communication and data exchange between traders and customs authorities.
The second group, "Customs Digital Public Services", includes six Business Service ABBs: "Economic Operator management and accreditation", "Economic Operators Registry management", "Compliance verification management", "Procedure Automation System", "Procedures registry management", and "Computerised Transit". These services represent various digital public services provided by customs, such as the management and accreditation of economic operators, the management of compliance verification, and the automation of procedures.
The motivation behind this view is to leverage digital technologies to enhance trade facilitation, ensure compliance with customs regulations, and promote efficient and secure cross-border trade within the customs environment. By reducing paperwork, improving accuracy, and expediting procedures, these digital solutions contribute to a more efficient and effective customs environment.

view.name: TVA-Functional Architecture Principles viewpoint
view.documentation:

By aligning architecture principles with application layer view functional components, solutions architects ensure consistency, enhance performance and scalability, promote reusability and maintainability, and support regulatory compliance. This alignment leads to the creation of robust and efficient applications within the application layer, enabling seamless integration, optimal user experience, reduced maintenance effort, and adherence to legal and industry standards.
In summary, aligning Architecture principles with application layer view functional components ensures consistency, enhances performance and scalability, promotes reusability and maintainability, and supports regulatory compliance. By following these principles, solutions architects can design robust and efficient applications within the application layer.
