view.name: TVA-Governance Architecture Principles viewpoint
view.documentation:
The view connects Architecture principles to technical view and the governance components. It is a relevant aspect of solutions architecture. This view specifically examines how architecture principles influence the design and implementation of governance structures within the application layer of a solution.
Firstly, it establishes effective governance within the application layer. Architecture principles provide guidance on defining governance structures, policies, and processes for application and infrastructure development and management. By aligning governance components with these principles, solutions architects design a robust governance framework that promotes compliance, transparency, and accountability in application development, configuration, and operations. This alignment ensures proper control and management of applications, reducing risks and enhancing overall governance practices.
Secondly, aligning architecture principles with governance components supports optimized application development and deployment. Architecture principles often emphasize best practices for application design, scalability, and performance optimization. By incorporating these principles into the design and implementation of governance components, solutions architects establish mechanisms for enforcing design patterns, scalability approaches, and performance monitoring.

view.name: TV-Technical Agreements
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The [TV-Technical Agreements] view extends technical view application and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging various types of agreements, contracts, and specifications to ensure interoperability, collaboration, and service quality across different systems and organizations.
The view includes four types of Technical Agreements: Contract ABB, Grouping ABB, and Business Object ABB. The Contract ABB type includes the Technical Agreement, Technical Interoperability Agreement, and Service Level Agreement. These agreements formalize the framework for strategic and technological collaboration, ensure organizations operate under different technical frameworks, and outline the level of service provided and the metrics used to measure service quality, respectively.
The Grouping ABB type includes the API Technical Interoperability Agreement Solutions, BlockChain Technical Interoperability Agreement Catalogue, and Identity and Access Management Technical Interoperability Agreement Solutions. These groupings provide a collection of technical specifications and standards for building and consuming APIs, ensuring interoperability using blockchain technology, and managing identity and access, respectively.
The Business Object ABB type includes the BlockChain Governance, Hybrid Blockchain Governance, Public BlockChain Governance (permissionless), and Private BlockChain Governance (permissioned). These objects provide the framework and mechanisms for effective collaboration and interoperability using blockchain technology.
The elements within these agreements, contracts, and specifications have relationships with each other based on their function and purpose. For example, the API Technical Interoperability Agreement Solutions grouping includes various Contract ABB elements like OpenAPI, RESTful API, GraphQL, gRPC, JSON-RPC, Simple Object Access Protocol, and OData. These elements provide the technical specifications for building and consuming APIs, enabling interoperability between different systems.
Similarly, the BlockChain Technical Interoperability Agreement Catalogue grouping includes the BlockChain IoP Agreement Contract ABB and the BlockChain Governance, Hybrid Blockchain Governance, Public BlockChain Governance (permissionless), and Private BlockChain Governance (permissioned) Business Object ABB elements. These elements provide the framework and mechanisms for ensuring interoperability using blockchain technology.
The motivation behind these elements and their relationships is to provide a comprehensive framework for leveraging technical agreements, contracts, and specifications to ensure interoperability, collaboration, and service quality across different systems and organizations. This framework enables organizations to identify common interests, prioritize policy dialogue, and develop the necessary tools for strategic and technological collaboration.

view.name: TVA-Dataspace Enablers
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE:
The EIRA approach for Data Spaces emphasises a decentralised model where no centralised elements, such as data lakes or data warehouses, are used to process or store the data. Instead, data is maintained and managed by the participants within the data space itself. This approach ensures that control over the data remains with the original data owners, fostering trust, data sovereignty, and compliance with data protection regulations. Through the EIRA/eGovERA Data Space approach, participants share data, allowing for collaboration without the need for centralised storage or processing hubs, thereby promoting a more distributed and flexible data management ecosystem.
The [TVA-Dataspace Enablers] view extends technical view application and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging various elements and their relationships to enable data integration, management, and usage. This view is composed of several Diagram Model-group ABBs, each containing multiple Application Service ABBs, and a Grouping ABB named [Dataspace Enablers].
The [App Store / Extensions / User Workflows] group includes three services: [Data Integration], [Data Integration Plugins Manager], and [Data Extraction, Transformation and Loading]. These services facilitate the process of combining data from multiple sources into a unified view, managing plugins within a data integration system, and extracting, transforming, and loading data into a target data store.
The [Event Driven / NRT] group contains the [Message Broker] service, which acts as an intermediary for asynchronous message-based communication between different applications.
The [Vocabulary Management] group includes the [Vocabulary Hub] service, a centralized repository for managing and providing access to a wide range of vocabularies or terminologies.
The [Trust] group contains the [Privacy] service, which enables functionalities such as storing, securing, anonymising, pseudonymising, rectifying and erasing personal data.
The [Identity Provider] group includes three services: [Centralized Identity Management], [Decentralized Identity Management], and [Identity Management]. These services manage and control user identities and access rights in both centralized and decentralized manners.
The [Monitoring] group contains the [Observability] service, which provides insights into the internal state and behavior of a system by analyzing its external outputs.
The [Dataspace Enablers] group includes the [Dataspace], [Dataspace Connector], [Dataspace Connector Provider], and [Dataspace Connector Consumer] services. These services support the creation and management of a dataspace, a virtual space for integrating, transforming, and making available data.
The [Contract Negotiation] group includes the [Data Contract], [Data Policy], and [Data Governance] services, which manage the availability, usability, integrity, and security of data within an organization.
The [Service Discovery and Registry], [Service Registry], [Data Catalogue Management], [Dataset Catalogue], and [Federated Data Catalogue Management] services enable the implementation of public digital services, organize metadata about data assets, and manage data catalogues.
The [Data Analytics and Quality] group includes the [Data Analytics] and [Data Quality] services, which analyze data and ensure its accuracy, completeness, consistency, and up-to-dateness.
The view also includes several Archimate Diagram-model ABBs that represent the motivation behind various elements, and Diagram Model-connection ABBs that represent the relationships between these elements.

view.name: OV-Customs Functional Architecture Principles viewpoint
view.documentation:
The Organizational-Functional Architecture Principles view is a crucial aspect of solutions architecture, as it directly influences the implementation of solutions within an organization's functional layers. This view focuses on aligning the design and implementation of solutions with the goals, requirements, and processes of the organization.
Aligning the Organizational-Functional Architecture Principles view with the organizational building blocks brings several benefits. Firstly, it ensures consistency and coherence across different functional areas within the organization. By defining and adhering to architecture principles, solutions architects establish a standardized approach that allows for seamless integration and interoperability between various building blocks. This consistency fosters effective communication and collaboration among departments and teams, promoting efficient business processes and operations.
Secondly, aligning the Organizational-Functional Architecture Principles view supports the scalability and adaptability of solutions. The architecture principles provide guidelines for designing modular, flexible, and reusable solutions. By considering the specific requirements and characteristics of each organizational building block, solutions architects can design solutions that can easily accommodate future changes and expansions. This scalability and adaptability enable the organization to respond to evolving business needs, reducing the time and resources required for future modifications.
Furthermore, aligning the Organizational-Functional Architecture Principles view enhances governance and decision-making processes within the organization. The architecture principles serve as a reference for making design decisions, ensuring that solutions align with the strategic objectives and priorities of the organization. By considering the unique characteristics and requirements of each building block, solutions architects can make informed choices that optimize resource utilization and support the overall organizational strategy.

Secondly, aligning the Organizational Governance Architecture Principles view supports effective communication and collaboration among stakeholders. The architecture principles provide guidelines for structuring roles, responsibilities, and decision-making processes within the governance building blocks. By considering the principles that influence these building blocks, solutions architects can design governance structures that facilitate clear lines of authority, information flow, and decision rights. This alignment fosters better coordination, accountability, and efficiency in governance activities across the organization.

view.name: OV-Duties Calculation and payment [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The OV-Duties Calculation and payment [Motivation] view extends the Organisational view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging the elements involved in the process of duties calculation and payment. This view is represented by the Diagram Model-group ABB named "Duties Calculation and payment".
The main capability of this model is the "Duties Calculation and payment" (DBC), which is a Capability SBB. This capability is supported by various Business Service ABBs, which include "Economic Operators Registry management", "Determination of the economic value of goods declared for importation", "Origin Registry management", "Customs declarations", "Classification of goods", "EU Customs Trader Portal", "Customs Decisions system", "Procedure Automation System", "Tariff Suspensions", "Goods flow analysis and simulations", "Intra-EU purchases and sales", "Duties calculation and payment", and "Duties guarantee management". These services represent the digital public services that facilitate the duties calculation and payment process.
The information required for these services is represented by Business Object ABBs, which include "Imports information", "Combined nomenclature", "Exports information", "Economic value Information", "Binding Tariffs Information", "Classification of goods Information", "Guarantee Information", "Origin of goods Information", "Economic Operators Information", and "Duties calculation Information". These objects provide the necessary data for the services to function effectively.
The motivation behind this view is to provide a clear and detailed representation of the elements involved in the duties calculation and payment process. This includes the capabilities, services, and information required to facilitate this process. By understanding these elements and their relationships, organizations can better manage and optimize the duties calculation and payment process.

view.name: OV-Export procedure [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The OV-Export procedure [Motivation] view extends the Organisational view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging the Export Procedure, which is a Diagram Model-group ABB. This procedure consists of various Business Service ABBs and Business Object ABBs that work together to manage and facilitate the export process.
The Business Service ABBs include Economic Operators Registry management, Origin Registry management, Customs declarations, Classification of goods, EU Customs information exchange, Goods flow analysis and simulations, Duties calculation and payment, and Duties guarantee management. These services are digital public services that handle different aspects of the export procedure, from managing registries and declarations to classifying goods and calculating duties.
The Business Object ABBs include Duties calculation Information, Economic Operators Information, Threads and fraudulent actions Information, Classification of goods Information, Guarantee Information, Origin of goods Information, Internal logistic Information, Binding Tariffs Information, Workforce information, Economic value Information, Special Procedures Information, Combined nomenclature, Customs partners Information, Imports information, and Economic Operators Registration and Identification number (EORI). These objects represent different types of information that are used and produced during the export procedure.
The Export Procedure capability SBB represents the ability to carry out the export procedure. This capability is crucial for the functioning of the export process and is supported by the various services and information objects mentioned above.
The relationships between these elements are not explicitly stated in the JSON, but it can be inferred that the Business Service ABBs use the Business Object ABBs to carry out their functions. For example, the Duties calculation and payment service might use the Duties calculation Information object to calculate the duties for a particular export. Similarly, the Economic Operators Registry management service might use the Economic Operators Information object to manage the registry of economic operators. The Export Procedure capability SBB, in turn, relies on all these services and information objects to carry out the export procedure.
The motivation behind this view is to provide a comprehensive understanding of the export procedure and the various elements involved in it. This understanding can help in identifying potential improvements and efficiencies in the export process.

view.name: OV-Transit procedure [Traceability]
view.documentation:

The Transit procedure is further broken down into several capabilities and services. The primary capability is also named "Transit procedure" and is represented as a Capability SBB. This capability is the driving force behind the transit procedure and serves as the main motivation for the other elements in the view.
Several Business Service ABBs are also part of the Transit procedure. These include "Determination of the economic value of goods declared for importation", "Origin Registry management", "Analysis Management", "Duties calculation and payment", "Duties guarantee management", "Computerised Transit", "Customs declarations", "Procedure Automation System", and "Classification of goods". Each of these services plays a crucial role in the transit procedure and contributes to its overall functionality.
The Transit procedure also involves several Business Object ABBs. These include "Duties calculation Information", "Imports information", "Exports information", "Special Procedures Information", "Economic value Information", "Origin of goods Information", "Combined nomenclature", "Classification of goods Information", and "Economic Operators Information". These objects represent the various types of information that are processed and managed during the transit procedure.
The relationships between these elements are crucial for the functioning of the Transit procedure. The Capability SBB motivates the Business Service ABBs, which in turn manage and process the Business Object ABBs. This interconnectedness ensures the smooth operation of the transit procedure and allows for efficient management of goods transit.

Digital business capabilities represent the technological functions and capacities required to deliver services in a digital environment. The Cooperation between Customs laboratories contains several elements that are crucial for its operation. These elements include Business Services ABBs, Business Objects ABBs, and a Capability SBB.
The Business Services ABBs include "Laboratories registry management", "Determination of the economic value of goods declared for importation", "Classification of goods", and "Goods flow analysis and simulations". The Business Objects ABBs include "Combined nomenclature", "Economic Operators Information", "Classification of goods Information", and "Laboratories information". These objects represent the information that is managed and used by the customs laboratories.
The Capability SBB is "Cooperation between Customs laboratories", which represents the ability of the customs laboratories to cooperate and work together.
The motivation behind this view is to provide a comprehensive framework that enables effective cooperation between customs laboratories. This is achieved by clearly defining the services provided by the laboratories, the information they manage and use, and their capability to cooperate. This framework is crucial for ensuring that the customs laboratories can effectively carry out their duties and responsibilities.
In terms of relations, the Business Services ABBs and Business Objects ABBs are related to the Capability SBB. This means that the services provided by the laboratories and the information they manage and use are directly linked to their ability to cooperate. This relationship is crucial for ensuring effective cooperation between the customs laboratories.

In addition to these services, the model-group also contains several business object ABBs, which represent various types of information. The relationships between these elements are crucial to the functioning of the Guarantee model-group. The Guarantee capability SBB is the central element that the other elements revolve around. The business services use the business objects as data to perform their functions. The motivation behind this model-group is to provide a comprehensive framework for managing guarantees. By having a clear structure and defined roles for each element, the model-group can effectively manage guarantees and ensure that all necessary services are provided.
