view.name: OV-Information Base
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The OV-Information Base view extends Organisational view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging business objects and grouping ABBs to support the delivery of digital public services.
The view consists of two main elements: 'Information' and 'Business Agnostic Business Information Base'. 'Information' is a Business Object ABB that describes business facts, assets, or opinions that are exchanged in the context of a digital public service to support its delivery. This information is enacted via interpretation rules (expressed in an ontology) of data and considering knowledge of a given context. Examples include an invoice, a medical prescription, a driving license.
The 'Business Agnostic Business Information Base' is a Grouping ABB that serves as a catalogue for various Business Object ABBs. These include 'Payment', 'Transaction', 'Identification', 'Qualification', 'Audit trail', 'Access rights', 'Profile', 'Message', 'Availability', 'Digital Signature', 'Document', 'Security Measure', 'Location', 'Invoice', 'Contracting authority', 'Economic operator', 'Digital Asset', 'Credential', 'Data Quality', and 'Distribution list'. Each of these represents a specific type of business information that is essential for the functioning of the digital public service.
The view also includes a 'Customs Information Base', which is another Grouping ABB. This base contains specific Business Object ABBs related to customs operations, such as 'Economic Operators Registration and Identification number (EORI)', 'Free circulation requirement information', 'Laboratories information', 'Threads and fraudulent actions Information', 'Duties calculation Information', 'Imports information', 'Combined nomenclature', 'Workforce information', 'Classification of goods Information', 'Temporary storage Information', 'Exports information', 'Special Procedures Information', 'Binding Tariffs Information', 'Guarantee Information', 'Economic Operators Information', 'Customs partners Information', 'Economic value Information', 'Internal logistic Information', and 'Origin of goods Information'.
The relations between these elements are not explicitly defined in the JSON, but it can be inferred that the 'Business Agnostic Business Information Base' and 'Customs Information Base' are subsets of the 'Information' element, as they provide specific types of information needed for the digital public service. The motivation behind this structure is to provide a comprehensive and organized view of all the information elements involved in the service, facilitating their management and utilization.

view.name: OV-Digital Business Capabilities Map
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The OV-Digital Business Capabilities Catalogue view extends Organisational view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging digital capabilities in public administration. This view is composed of two main elements: "Digital Business Capability" and two Grouping ABBs - "Business Agnostic Digital Business Capabilities Map" and "Customs Digital Business Capabilities Map".
The "Digital Business Capability" is a Capability ABB that corresponds to an ability implemented in a system to enable public administrations to perform an administrative function. This capability does not contain any sub-elements.
The "Business Agnostic Digital Business Capabilities Map" is a Grouping ABB that encompasses a set of Capability SBBs. These capabilities include "Electronic Identification", "Qualification Management", "Digital Payments", "Digital Procurement", "Digital Communication", "Digital Exchange", "Digital Invoicing", "Data Management", "Multimedia Management", "Contact Management", "Case and Workflow Management", "Knowledge Management", "Digital Twin", and "Artificial Intelligence". Each of these capabilities represents a specific digital business capability that can be leveraged by public administrations.
The "Customs Digital Business Capabilities Map" is another Grouping ABB that includes a set of Capability SBBs related to customs operations. These capabilities include "Compliance requirements checks", "Customs cooperation", "Import procedure", "Guarantee", "Tariffs registry management", "Preservation of cargo information", "Cooperation between Customs and Postal Operators", "Transit procedure", "Authorised Economic Operator accreditation", "Risk analysis", "Cooperation between Customs laboratories", "Special procedure", "Laboratories management", "MS' Customs organization management", "Export procedure", and "Duties Calculation and payment", and "Expeditions controls". Each of these capabilities represents a specific digital business capability that can be leveraged by customs administrations.
The relationships between these elements are not explicitly defined in the JSON data, but it can be inferred that the Capability SBBs within each Grouping ABB are related in that they contribute to the overall digital business capabilities of public or customs administrations. The motivation for these elements and their relationships is to provide a comprehensive framework for leveraging digital capabilities in public administration, enabling more efficient and effective operations.

view.name: OV-Digital Public Services Catalogue
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The OV-Digital Public Services Catalogue view extends Organisational view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging the digital transformation of public services. The view is composed of two main elements: the "Digital Public Service Catalogue" and the "Business Agnostic Digital Public Services Catalogue".
The "Digital Public Service Catalogue" is a Business Object ABB that enables the index of active digital public services, and their descriptions, provided by a public administration. This ABB is a key interoperability enabler for sharing and provisioning, as well as reusing and consuming of front-office public services.
The "Business Agnostic Digital Public Services Catalogue" is a Grouping ABB that includes a variety of Business Service ABBs. These services range from ePayment, Audit, eArchiving, eDelivery, eQualification, eTranslation, Data Extraction, Transformation and Loading, Data Analytics, Delegation of Power, Workflow Management, Knowledge Management, eNotification, eIdentification, Digital Collaboration, Waiting list Management, Open Data Management, Anonymisation, eSignature, Secure Access Control, Content Management, Log Management, eInvoicing, eTendering, Contact Management, Forms Management, Data Exchange, Digital Inmutability, Business Intelligence, Compliance Testing, Data Space, to Data Space Participant. Each of these services represents a specific digital public service provided by the public administration.
The view also includes a "Customs Digital Public Services Catalogue", which is another Grouping ABB. This catalogue includes Business Service ABBs that are specific to customs operations, such as Economic Operators Registry management, EU Customs Trader Portal, Analysis Management, (Internal) Customs logistics management, Centralised Clearance for Import, Determination of the economic value of goods declared for importation, Tariff Registry management, Applications and Requests, Compliance verification management, Duties guarantee management, Origin Registry management, Customs Decisions system, Customs organizational structure management, Duties calculation and payment, Partner authorization, Customs declarations, Procedure Automation System, Preservation of cargo control, Intra-EU purchases and sales, Notification of Arrival, Presentation Notification and Temporary Storage, Classification of goods, Procedures registry management, Tariff Suspensions, Computerised Transit, Risk analysis, Laboratories registry management, EU Customs information exchange, Goods flow analysis and simulations, and Economic Operator management and accreditation.
In summary, the OV-Digital Public Services Catalogue view provides a comprehensive framework for understanding and managing the digital transformation of public services, with a particular focus on interoperability and the sharing and reusing of services.

view.name: OV-Data Spaces
view.documentation:
The Organisational view models the most salient Architecture Building Blocks and Solution Building blocks that shall be considered in order to support organisational interoperability among providers and users of a public service.
Narrative: The delivery of public services involves various organizations playing different roles within the ecosystem. Public service providers, acting as suppliers, offer public services to citizens, businesses, and public administrations, who act as consumers of these services. The specific public services are documented in public service catalogues, which serve as a reference for service portfolio management. Public service providers can delegate the delivery of these services to public service delivery agents who act on their behalf. To ensure effective service delivery, public service providers can enter into interoperability agreements that define the agreed-upon approach to delivering public services to users.
The delivery of public services relies on the utilization of business capabilities and the exchange of business information. Business capabilities represent the operational functions required to deliver the services, while the exchange of business information facilitates the transfer of relevant data between the involved parties. The exchanged business information is specific to each instance and is governed by business rules derived from organizational interoperability enablers such as organizational structures, procedures, policies, and skills.
Interoperability governance is overseen by the interoperability organizational authority, responsible for establishing and enforcing governance practices. This authority influences the interoperability strategy, which in turn implements the interoperability framework. Interoperability skills, a specialized form of organizational skills, enable organizations to excel in interoperability and effectively participate in the ecosystem.
Security also plays a crucial role in the delivery of digital public services. A security framework, which is a specific form of a security policy, addresses the organization's security-related aspects, ensuring the protection of sensitive information and adherence to security standards.
To support the design and implementation of digital public services, additional solution building blocks are extended. These include organizational agreements, a digital governance plan, a digital public service catalogue, information management, and digital business capabilities. These building blocks provide specific functionalities and capabilities to enhance the development and deployment of digital public services, aligning them with the overarching organizational framework.
Overall, the organizational layer of the solution architecture template outlines the roles, agreements, processes, and governance mechanisms necessary for effective delivery of public services. It emphasizes the importance of interoperability, security, and specialized skills, while incorporating additional solution building blocks to enable the design and implementation of digital public services.

view.name: OV-Organisational Agreements
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The OV-Organisational Agreements view extends Organisational view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging various elements that are crucial for the functioning of an organisation. This view is designed to provide a detailed understanding of the organisational agreements and their associated elements.
The first element is the "Organisational Agreement", which is of the type "Contract ABB". The Organisational Agreement ABB is a Contract that enables any agreement to which the Organisation or any Restricted Subsidiary is a party pursuant. This implies that this contract is a binding agreement that the organisation or its restricted subsidiaries must adhere to.
The second element is the "Business Agnostic Organisational Agreement Catalogue", which is of the type "Grouping ABB". This catalogue is a collection of organisational agreements that are business-agnostic, meaning they are applicable regardless of the specific business context or industry. This catalogue includes a sub-element named "National Governance Models", which is of the type "Contract ABB". The National Governance Models are contracts that define the governance models at a national level.
The third element is the "Business Agnostic Organisational Agreement Solutions", which is also of the type "Grouping ABB". This element represents a collection of solutions that are business-agnostic and pertain to organisational agreements. This includes a sub-element named "Code of Conduct for Energy Efficiency in Data Centres", which is of the type "Contract SBB". This contract outlines the code of conduct for maintaining energy efficiency in data centres.
The relationships between these elements are defined by their hierarchical structure. The Organisational Agreement is a standalone element, while the Business Agnostic Organisational Agreement Catalogue and Business Agnostic Organisational Agreement Solutions are groupings that contain specific contracts. These contracts, namely the National Governance Models and the Code of Conduct for Energy Efficiency in Data Centres, are part of their respective groupings and contribute to the overall organisational agreements framework.
The motivation for this structure is to provide a comprehensive and structured view of the organisational agreements, allowing for a clear understanding of the various contracts and their implications. This helps in ensuring compliance and effective governance within the organisation.

view.name: SV-Customs Data Representation [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The SV-Customs Data Representation [Motivation] view extends Semantic view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging the elements of data representation and customs data format, representation, and syntax solutions.
The first element, named 'Data Representation', is of the type 'Representation ABB'. It describes the perceptible configuration of business information or a legal act. Representations can be classified in various ways, such as by medium (e.g., electronic or paper documents, audio, etc.) or format (HTML, ASCII, PDF, RTF, etc.). This element does not contain any sub-elements.
The second element, named 'Customs Data Format, Representation and Syntax Solutions', is of the type 'Grouping ABB'. This element groups together solutions related to customs data format, representation, and syntax. Within this grouping, there is a sub-element named 'EDIFACT', which is of the type 'Representation SBB'. EDIFACT, or 'CUSDEC', is a specific format used for customs declarations. It includes fields and structures for capturing information about import or export shipments, including details about goods, their classification, valuation, origin, and other customs-related information.
The relationship between the 'Data Representation' and 'Customs Data Format, Representation and Syntax Solutions' elements is not explicitly defined in the JSON. However, it can be inferred that 'Customs Data Format, Representation and Syntax Solutions' is a specific application of the general 'Data Representation' concept. The 'EDIFACT' sub-element, in turn, is a specific instance of the 'Customs Data Format, Representation and Syntax Solutions' grouping.
The motivation behind this view is to provide a structured way of representing and organizing data related to customs declarations, thereby facilitating more efficient and accurate data processing and decision-making.

view.name: SV-Agnostic Ontology Catalogue [Traceability]
view.documentation: Narrative: The "Semantic view - Agnostic Ontology Catalogue" viewpoint extends the semantic view and provides a comprehensive framework for organizing and managing agnostic ontologies within the digital ecosystem. This view associates the Business Agnostic Ontologies Catalogue with Digital Public Services and the Business Information Base from the application layer. Within this view, the Business Agnostic Ontologies Catalogue serves as a centralized repository for storing and categorizing a collection of agnostic ontologies. It acts as a catalogue of standardized concepts, relationships, and rules that are independent of specific business domains. The catalogue ensures that ontologies are easily discoverable, accessible, and reusable across different digital services and applications. The Digital Public Services, as part of the application layer, leverage the ontologies within the Business Agnostic Ontologies Catalogue to ensure consistent and meaningful representation of information and functionalities. These services align with the ontological concepts and relationships to enable seamless interactions, data exchange, and semantic interoperability among various digital public services. Furthermore, the Business Information Base complements the Business Agnostic Ontologies Catalogue by providing a structured repository of business-related information. It serves as a valuable resource for storing and accessing domain-specific data, supporting decision-making processes, and enabling the enrichment of ontologies within the catalogue. By associating the Business Agnostic Ontologies Catalogue with Digital Public Services and the Business Information Base, the "Semantic view - Agnostic Ontology Catalogue" facilitates the discovery, retrieval, and reuse of agnostic ontologies within the digital ecosystem. This view promotes the standardization and consistency of ontological concepts and relationships, allowing for effective semantic interoperability, data integration, and advanced functionalities such as semantic search and intelligent data processing. The agnostic nature of the ontologies within the catalogue allows for flexibility and adaptability across different business domains and digital public services. It enables organizations to leverage existing ontologies and avoid duplication of efforts, reducing complexity and promoting the consistency of information representation.

view.name: SV-Business Agnostic Data Models [Traceability]
view.documentation:
Narrative: The "Semantic view - Business Agnostic Data Models" viewpoint extends the semantic view provides a comprehensive framework for organizing and utilizing business agnostic data models within the digital ecosystem. This view associates the Agnostic Data Models with Digital Public Services from the application layer.
Within this view, Agnostic Data Models represent standardized and domain-independent structures for organizing and representing data. These models define the entities, attributes, relationships, and rules that are applicable across different business domains, ensuring consistency and interoperability in data representation and exchange.
Digital Public Services, as part of the application layer, leverage the Agnostic Data Models to ensure uniformity and coherence in data organization and management. These services align their data structures, operations, and interactions with the agnostic data models, enabling seamless integration, data consistency, and semantic interoperability among different digital public services.
By associating the Agnostic Data Models with Digital Public Services, the "Semantic view - Business Agnostic Data Models" facilitates standardized data modeling and data management practices. This view supports effective data integration, semantic interoperability, and advanced functionalities within the digital ecosystem.
The agnostic nature of the data models allows for flexibility and adaptability across different business domains and digital public services. It promotes reusability, reduces redundancy, and supports consistent and efficient data representation and exchange.

view.name: SV-Business Agnostic Syntax Mapping [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The SV-Data Syntax Mapping Catalogue [Motivation] view extends Semantic view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging the elements in the given JSON. This view is designed to bridge the gap between different systems or data models, ensuring that data remains accurate and usable when transferred from a source to a destination.
The JSON contains two main elements: "Business Agnostic Business Information Base" and "Data Syntax Mapping Catalogue".
The "Business Agnostic Business Information Base" is a Diagram Model-group ABB. It is a business-agnostic model that serves as a base for business information. This base includes a sub-element named "Availability", which is a Business Object ABB. The "Availability" object represents availability information, and it does not contain any sub-elements.
The second main element in the JSON is the "Data Syntax Mapping Catalogue", which is a Data Object ABB. The description indicates that this catalogue serves as a bridge between two systems or data models. It is designed to ensure that data remains accurate and usable when it is moved from a source to a destination. This element does not contain any sub-elements.
The relationship between these two main elements is not explicitly defined in the JSON. However, based on the descriptions, it can be inferred that the "Data Syntax Mapping Catalogue" may use the "Business Agnostic Business Information Base" to ensure the accuracy and usability of data during transfer. The motivation behind this relationship is to facilitate efficient data transfer between different systems or data models, thereby enhancing the overall data management process.

view.name: SV-Data Mapping Catalogue [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The SV-Data Mapping Catalogue [Motivation] view extends Semantic view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging the business agnostic business information base and the data mapping catalogue.
The first element in this view is the 'Business Agnostic Business Information Base', which is a Diagram Model-group ABB. This base is a general-purpose business information base that is not tied to any specific business context or domain. It contains two sub-elements: 'Availability' and 'Digital Asset', both of which are Business Object ABBs.
'Availability' is a business object that represents the availability information. This could include data about the availability of resources, services, or any other business elements. The 'Digital Asset' business object represents the digital asset information. This could include data about digital resources such as software, digital media, or any other digital assets.
The second main element in this view is the 'Data Mapping Catalogue', which is a Data Object ABB. This catalogue is a data object that aims to index an inventory of rules or procedures on how data from different sources and domains can be linked and integrated. This could include mapping rules, transformation rules, integration procedures, or any other relevant information.
The relationship between these elements is that the 'Data Mapping Catalogue' uses the data from the 'Business Agnostic Business Information Base' to create a comprehensive and integrated view of the business data. This allows for a more effective and efficient use of the data, as it can be easily linked and integrated across different sources and domains.
The motivation behind this view is to provide a comprehensive framework for leveraging business data. By using a business agnostic business information base and a data mapping catalogue, businesses can effectively manage their data and use it to drive business decisions and actions. This can lead to improved business performance and competitiveness.

view.name: SV-Agnostic Reference Data [Traceability]
view.documentation: Narrative: The "Semantic view - Agnostic Reference Data" viewpoint extends the semantic view and provides a comprehensive framework for managing and leveraging agnostic reference data within the digital ecosystem. This view associates the Agnostic Reference Data with Digital Public Services and the Business Information Base from the application layer. Within this view, the Agnostic Reference Data acts as a centralized repository for standardized and commonly used reference data across different business domains. It includes data elements such as codes, classifications, and identifiers that are independent of specific contexts. The agnostic nature of the reference data ensures consistency and interoperability across various digital services and applications. The Digital Public Services, as part of the application layer, rely on the Agnostic Reference Data to ensure uniformity and accuracy in data representation and exchange. These services align their data structures and operations with the reference data, enabling seamless integration, data consistency, and semantic interoperability among different digital public services. Furthermore, the Business Information Base complements the Agnostic Reference Data by providing a repository of business-related information that relies on the reference data. It serves as a valuable resource for storing and accessing domain-specific data, facilitating decision-making processes, and enabling the enrichment of reference data within the digital ecosystem. By associating the Agnostic Reference Data with Digital Public Services and the Business Information Base, the "Semantic view - Agnostic Reference Data" promotes the standardization and consistency of reference data within the digital ecosystem. This view ensures the availability and accessibility of accurate and up-to-date reference data, enabling effective data integration, semantic interoperability, and advanced functionalities in digital public services. The use of agnostic reference data allows for flexibility and adaptability across different business domains and digital public services. It facilitates data harmonization, reduces redundancy, and enables consistent data interpretation and exchange across applications and systems.

node.label: Not clear if it is an SBB in itself. It seems to be a broad description for Authority Tables and other asstets managed by the Publications Office

view.name: SV-Business Agnostic High Value Dataset [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The SV-High Value Datasets [Motivation] view extends Semantic view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging high-value datasets and business information. This view is composed of several elements, each with unique characteristics and relationships.
The first element, "Business Agnostic High Value Dataset Solutions," is a Grouping ABB that serves as a catalogue for various high-value datasets. These datasets are divided into six Data Object SBBs: "Geospatial High Value Dataset," "Business-related data High Value Dataset," "Metereology High Value Dataset," "Mobility High Value Dataset," "Statistics High Value Dataset," and "Earth Observation Data High Value Dataset." Each of these datasets contains specific data related to their respective fields, such as INSPIRE themes, reference parcels, agricultural parcels, basic company information, records, financial statements, weather data, river information services data, statistical data on select legal acts, and environmental information.
The second element, "Business Agnostic Business Information Base," is a Diagram Model-group ABB that contains three Business Object ABBs: "Availability," "Data Quality," and "Document." These objects provide information on the availability of the datasets, the quality of the data, and any related documents.
The third element, "Dataset," is a Data Object ABB that represents a collection of related data organized and presented in a structured format. This element serves as a foundation for the high-value datasets.
The final element, "High Value Dataset," is a Data Object ABB that represents datasets with the potential to generate significant socio-economic or environmental benefits, innovative services, assist in generating revenues, and be combined with other datasets. This element highlights the value and potential benefits of the datasets.
The relationships between these elements are crucial for understanding the motivation behind the SV-High Value Datasets [Motivation] view. The high-value datasets are grouped under the "Business Agnostic High Value Dataset Solutions" and are supported by the "Business Agnostic Business Information Base," which provides necessary information about the datasets. The "Dataset" and "High Value Dataset" elements further emphasize the importance and value of these datasets.

view.name: SV-Forms Structure [Traceability]
view.documentation: Narrative: The "Semantic view - Forms Structure" extends semantic view and provides a comprehensive framework for designing and managing the structure of forms within the digital ecosystem. This view associates the Forms Structure with the Business Information Base and Digital Public Services from the application layer. Within this view, the Forms Structure defines the organization, layout, and components of digital forms used for data collection and input. It ensures a consistent and standardized approach to form design, enhancing user experience, and enabling efficient data capture. The Business Information Base, as part of the application layer, relies on the Forms Structure to ensure effective data collection and management. It utilizes the defined forms structure to design and implement forms that capture domain-specific data accurately and comprehensively. Digital Public Services leverage the Forms Structure to ensure consistent form design and data collection across different services. These services align their data models, operations, and interactions with the defined forms structure, enhancing user engagement and facilitating accurate data entry within the digital ecosystem. By associating the Forms Structure with the Business Information Base and Digital Public Services, the "Semantic view - Forms Structure" promotes standardized form design and enables efficient data capture and management. This view ensures consistency in form layout and components, improves data quality, and enhances user satisfaction within the context of digital public services. The defined forms structure allows for streamlined data collection, reducing errors, and ensuring data completeness. It provides a user-friendly interface for capturing data, guiding users through the necessary fields and data entry requirements.

view.name: SV-Customs Controlled Vocabularies [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The SV-Customs Controlled Vocabularies [Motivation] view extends Semantic view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging standardized vocabularies and taxonomies in the context of customs operations and trade facilitation. This view is composed of three main elements: 'Customs Vocabularies', 'Customs Information Base', and 'Controlled Vocabulary'.
The 'Customs Vocabularies' element is a Grouping ABB that encompasses three Data Objects: 'Registered Organisation Vocabulary', 'National Customs Specific Taxonomy', and 'Combined Nomenclature'. These vocabularies provide a standardized set of terms and concepts for representing and describing registered organizations, customs-related data, regulations, and procedures unique to a nation's trade and customs environment, and a tool for classifying goods to meet the requirements of the Common Customs TariffEN and of the EU external trade statistics.
The 'Customs Information Base' is a Diagram Model-group ABB that includes a variety of Business Objects such as 'Economic Operators Information', 'Free circulation requirement information', 'Imports information', 'Laboratories information', 'Combined nomenclature', 'Exports information', 'Customs partners Information', 'Economic value Information', 'Origin of goods Information', and 'Workforce information'. These Business Objects represent different types of information that are crucial for customs operations and trade facilitation.
The 'Controlled Vocabulary' is a Data Object ABB that represents a carefully curated set of terms used to describe concepts or objects in the customs and trade domain. This standardized list of terms is used to ensure consistency and accuracy in the indexing, searching, and retrieval of information.
The relationship between these elements is such that the 'Customs Vocabularies' and 'Controlled Vocabulary' provide the standardized terms and concepts that are used in the 'Customs Information Base' to ensure consistent and accurate representation of customs-related information. This facilitates efficient customs operations, enhances trade facilitation, and supports accurate reporting and analysis.

view.name: SV-Agnostic Ontologies [Traceability]
view.documentation:
Narrative: The "semantic view - Agnostic Ontologies" viewpoint extends the semantic view and provides a comprehensive framework for representing and organizing knowledge within the digital ecosystem. This view associates the Business Agnostic Ontologies with Digital Public Services and the Business Information Base from the application layer. Within this view, the Business Agnostic Ontologies serve as foundational structures for representing and defining common concepts, relationships, and rules that are independent of specific business domains. These ontologies provide a shared understanding and semantic framework that enables interoperability, data integration, and semantic reasoning across different digital services and applications.
The Digital Public Services, as part of the application layer, leverage the Business Agnostic Ontologies to ensure consistent and meaningful representation of information and functionalities. These services align with the ontological concepts and relationships to enable seamless interactions, data exchange, and interoperability among various digital public services.
Furthermore, the Business Information Base complements the Business Agnostic Ontologies by providing a structured repository of business-related information. It serves as a valuable resource for storing and accessing domain-specific data, facilitating data sharing, and supporting decision-making processes within digital public services.
By associating the Business Agnostic Ontologies with Digital Public Services and the Business Information Base, the "semantic view - Agnostic Ontologies" enables a standardized and coherent representation of knowledge and information within the digital ecosystem. This view promotes semantic interoperability, enhances data integration, and supports advanced functionalities such as semantic search, intelligent recommendations, and context-aware decision-making.

view.name: SV-Agnostic Data Policies and Contracts- Data Space [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The SV-Data Space Policies and Contracts [Motivation] view extends Semantic view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging the elements of Data Space Policies and Contracts and Business Agnostic Business Information Base.
The Data Space Policies and Contracts is a Grouping ABB that serves as a catalogue for the elements it contains. This catalogue includes two Data Object ABBs: Data Policy and Data Contract. The Data Policy is a standalone element with no sub-elements, and it represents the policies that govern the data in the data space. The Data Contract, also a standalone element, represents the contracts that dictate the terms and conditions of data usage within the data space.
The Business Agnostic Business Information Base is a Diagram Model-group ABB that contains a collection of Business Object ABBs. These objects include Availability, Digital Asset, Credential, Access rights, and Transaction. Each of these elements represents different types of information that are business-agnostic, meaning they are not specific to any one business or industry.
The Availability object represents information about the availability of data or services. The Digital Asset object represents information about digital assets, which could include digital files, software, or other digital resources. The Credential object represents information about credentials, which could include usernames, passwords, or other forms of identification. The Access rights object represents information about access rights, which dictate who can access certain data or services. Lastly, the Transaction object represents information about transactions, which could include financial transactions, data transactions, or other types of exchanges.
The relationships between these elements are not explicitly defined in the JSON, but it can be inferred that the Data Space Policies and Contracts catalogue governs the data represented by the Business Object ABBs in the Business Agnostic Business Information Base. This governance could include setting policies for how the data is used (Data Policy) and establishing contracts for data usage (Data Contract). The motivation behind this structure is to provide a comprehensive framework for managing data in a way that is not specific to any one business or industry, allowing for flexibility and adaptability.

view.name: SV-Data Model [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The SV-Data Model [Motivation] view extends Semantic view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging the elements in the JSON data. The JSON data contains three main elements: "Business Agnostic Data Model Solutions", "Business Agnostic Business Information Base", and "Data Model".
The "Business Agnostic Data Model Solutions" is a Grouping ABB type element that encompasses two sub-elements: "Common Data Model" and "eProcurement Data Model Solutions". The "Common Data Model" is a Data Object SBB type element that represents an ontology based on the FRBR model (Functional Requirements for Bibliographic Records) using RDF(S)/OWL technologies. It is capable of representing relationships between the resource types managed by the Publications Office and their views, all within the scope of the FRBR model.
The "eProcurement Data Model Solutions" is another Grouping ABB type element that includes the "ESPD-EDM" as a sub-element. The "ESPD-EDM" is a Data Object SBB type element representing the European Single Procurement Document (ESPD), a standardized form used in public procurement processes within the European Union (EU). It serves as a preliminary self-declaration by suppliers, demonstrating their eligibility and suitability to participate in public procurement procedures across EU member states.
The "Business Agnostic Business Information Base" is a Diagram Model-group ABB type element that includes three sub-elements: "Message", "Document", and "Data Quality". Each of these sub-elements is a Business Object ABB type element representing different types of business information.
Finally, the "Data Model" is a Data Object ABB type element that aims to be a collection of entities, their properties, and the relationships among them. It focuses on formally representing a domain, a concept, or a real-world thing.
The relationships among these elements are defined by their hierarchical structure in the JSON data. The motivation behind this structure is to provide a comprehensive and structured representation of different types of data models and business information, facilitating their use in various business contexts.

view.name: SV-Customs Form Structure [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The SV-Customs Form Structure [Motivation] view extends Semantic view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging the structure and organization of customs forms and the information base related to customs.
The view is composed of three main elements: "Customs Forms Structure", "Customs Information Base", and "Forms Structure".
The "Customs Forms Structure" is a Grouping ABB that encompasses three Data Object SBBs: "BTI Application Form", "EUR.1 Movement Certificate", and "Single Administrative Document (SAD)". Each of these forms serves a specific purpose in the customs process, collecting and providing necessary information for customs authorities to make decisions regarding the classification, origin, and movement of goods.
The "BTI Application Form" is used to request an official binding decision from customs authorities regarding the classification of specific goods under the Harmonized System (HS). The "EUR.1 Movement Certificate" certifies the origin of goods and claims preferential treatment in international trade. The "Single Administrative Document (SAD)" is a form used for customs declarations in the EU and other countries, aiming to reduce the administrative burden and increase the standardisation and harmonisation of data collected on trade.
The "Customs Information Base" is a Diagram Model-group ABB that contains nine Business Object ABBs. These objects represent various types of information related to customs, including "Origin of goods Information", "Imports information", "Classification of goods Information", "Exports information", "Economic value Information", "Combined nomenclature", "Free circulation requirement information", "Economic Operators Registration and Identification number (EORI)", and "Economic Operators Information". Each of these objects provides crucial data for the customs process, contributing to the overall efficiency and effectiveness of customs operations.
The "Forms Structure" is a Data Object ABB that enables the implementation of the layout and organization of the fields, labels, and controls on a form used to collect or display data. This object plays a crucial role in ensuring the usability and functionality of the customs forms.
In terms of relations, the "Customs Forms Structure" and "Customs Information Base" are related in that the forms collect and provide the information represented by the Business Object ABBs in the information base. The "Forms Structure" is related to the "Customs Forms Structure" as it defines the layout and organization of the forms. The motivation behind this view is to provide a comprehensive and structured framework for managing and leveraging customs forms and related information, thereby enhancing the efficiency and effectiveness of customs operations.

view.name: SV-Data Mapping [Traceability]
view.documentation:
Narrative: The "Semantic view - Data Mapping" viewpoint extends semantic view and provides a comprehensive framework for managing and aligning data mappings within the digital ecosystem. This view associates the Data Mapping with the Business Information Base and Digital Public Services from the application layer. Within this view, Data Mapping involves the translation and transformation of data representations between different formats, structures, and systems. It enables seamless data integration, interoperability, and efficient data exchange across various applications and services.
The Business Information Base, as part of the application layer, serves as a repository of business-related information that relies on data mappings. It stores and manages data using mappings that ensure data consistency and compatibility, facilitating data sharing and decision-making processes. Digital Public Services leverage Data Mapping to ensure accurate and meaningful data exchange and integration. These services align their data models, operations, and interactions with the defined data mappings, enabling seamless integration, data consistency, and interoperability among different digital public services.
By associating the Data Mapping with the Business Information Base and Digital Public Services, the "Semantic view - Data Mapping" promotes standardized data mappings, facilitating efficient data integration and interoperability within the digital ecosystem. This view supports effective data exchange, consistent data representation, and advanced functionalities for digital public services.

view.name: SV-Controlled Vocabulary [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The SV-Controlled Vocabulary [Motivation] view extends Semantic view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging controlled vocabulary solutions in a business-agnostic manner. This view is composed of three main elements: Business Agnostic Controlled Vocabulary Solutions, Business Agnostic Business Information Base, and Controlled Vocabulary.
The Business Agnostic Controlled Vocabulary Solutions is a Grouping ABB that encompasses several Data Object SBBs. These include eGovernment Core Vocabularies, Core Assessment Vocabulary, Core Standards and Specifications Vocabulary, W3C Profiles Vocabulary, and EuroVoc. Each of these data objects represents a specific set of vocabularies or standards used for information exchange, assessment, and description of various data entities in a context-neutral manner. For instance, the eGovernment Core Vocabularies are simplified, reusable, and extensible data models that capture the fundamental characteristics of a data entity. Similarly, the Core Assessment Vocabulary defines what an 'Assessment' of 'assets' is and how to perform the assessment based on 'Criteria'.
The Business Agnostic Business Information Base is a Diagram Model-group ABB that includes two Business Object ABBs: Data Quality and Availability. These objects represent the quality and availability of the business information, respectively.
The Controlled Vocabulary is a Data Object ABB that enables a carefully curated set of terms used to describe concepts or objects in a specific field or domain. It is a standardized list of terms that are used to ensure consistency and accuracy in the indexing, searching, and retrieval of information.
The motivation behind this view is to provide a comprehensive and standardized framework for the use of controlled vocabularies in a business-agnostic manner. This ensures consistency and accuracy in the description, indexing, and retrieval of information across different business domains. It also facilitates the exchange of information and interoperability among various software solutions.

view.name: SV-Customs Base Registries [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The SV-Customs Base Registries [Motivation] view extends Semantic view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging data objects and business objects related to customs activities. This view is divided into three main elements: the Customs Base Registry, the Customs Information Base, and the Base Registry.
The Customs Base Registry is a Grouping ABB that encompasses six Data Object SBBs, each representing a different system or database used in customs activities. These include the REX - Registered Exporter system, EORI - Economic Operators Registration and Identification number, ICS (Import Control System), TARIC (Integrated Tariff of the European Union), VAT Information Exchange System (VIES), and AEO - Authorised Economic Operator. Each of these systems or databases serves a unique purpose in the customs process, from certifying the origin of goods and assigning unique identification numbers to economic operators, to enhancing customs control, providing tariff information, verifying VAT numbers, and recognizing businesses that meet certain criteria and demonstrate compliance with customs regulations and security standards.
The Customs Information Base is a Diagram Model-group ABB that includes nine Business Object ABBs, each representing a different type of information used in customs activities. These include Exports information, Imports information, Origin of goods Information, Economic value Information, Customs partners Information, Binding Tariffs Information, Economic Operators Registration and Identification number (EORI), Economic Operators Information, and Workforce information. These business objects provide essential information for customs activities, such as details about exports and imports, the origin of goods, economic value, customs partners, binding tariffs, registration and identification numbers for economic operators, information about economic operators, and workforce information.
The Base Registry is a Data Object ABB that refers to reliable sources of basic information that permits an efficient, secure, and transparent exchange of the data. This registry serves as a foundational element in the SV-Customs Base Registries [Motivation] view, providing the underlying data that supports the other elements in the view.
In summary, the SV-Customs Base Registries [Motivation] view provides a comprehensive framework for managing and leveraging data and information related to customs activities. It integrates various systems and databases, each serving a unique purpose in the customs process, and provides a wide range of essential information for customs activities. The Base Registry serves as the foundation for this view, providing reliable sources of basic information that enable efficient, secure, and transparent data exchange.

view.name: SV-Business Agnostic Metadata [Traceability]
view.documentation: Narartive: The "Semantic view - Business Agnostic Datasets" viewpoint extends semantic view and provides a comprehensive framework for managing and utilizing business agnostic datasets within the digital ecosystem. This view associates the Agnostic Datasets with the Business Information Base and Digital Public Services from the application layer. Within this view, Agnostic Datasets represent standardized collections of data that are independent of specific business domains. These datasets adhere to common data structures, formats, and semantics, enabling interoperability, data integration, and efficient data exchange across different digital services and applications. The Business Information Base, as part of the application layer, serves as a repository of business-related information that utilizes the Agnostic Datasets. It stores and manages domain-specific data within the standardized dataset structures, facilitating data consistency, accessibility, and sharing. Digital Public Services leverage the Agnostic Datasets to ensure uniformity and coherence in data representation and utilization. These services align their data models, operations, and interactions with the agnostic datasets, enabling seamless integration, data consistency, and semantic interoperability among different digital public services. By associating the Agnostic Datasets with the Business Information Base and Digital Public Services, the "Semantic view - Business Agnostic Datasets" promotes standardized data management practices and efficient data utilization within the digital ecosystem. This view supports data integration, semantic interoperability, and advanced functionalities for digital public services. The agnostic nature of the datasets allows for flexibility and adaptability across different business domains and digital public services. It enables reusability of data structures, reduces data duplication, and promotes consistent data representation and exchange.

view.name: SV-Dataset [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The SV-Dataset [Motivation] view extends Semantic view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging various types of data objects and their associated metadata. This view is primarily composed of three main elements: the Business Agnostic Dataset Catalogue, the Business Agnostic Business Information Base, and the Data Objects ABBs.
The Business Agnostic Dataset Catalogue is a Grouping ABB that contains several Data Object ABBs, each representing a specific type of metadata. These include Multimedia Object Metadata, Log Metadata, Translation Item Metadata, Transaction Metadata, Exchange Item Metadata, Tender Item Metadata, and Authorised Payment Methods Metadata. Each of these metadata types provides structured information about a specific aspect of data, such as multimedia assets, log events, translation items, transactions, exchange items, tender items, and authorized payment methods. The metadata helps in identifying, organizing, retrieving, analyzing, and managing the corresponding data assets, thereby enabling efficient data operations.
The Business Agnostic Business Information Base is a Diagram Model-group ABB that contains several Business Object ABBs. These represent various types of business information, including Location, Data Quality, Payment, Transaction, Message, Document, Audit Trail, and Availability. Each of these business objects provides specific business-related information, which is crucial for the operation and management of business activities.
The Data Objects ABBs include Dataset, Reference Data, and Master Data. The Dataset ABB represents a collection of related data organized in a structured format. The Reference Data ABB enables the definition of a set of values or codes used to categorize, classify, or describe data elements in a consistent and standardized way. The Master Data ABB enables the implementation of non-transactional information that plays a key role in the core operation of a business in public administrations and is re-used for multiple purposes.
The relationships among these elements are defined by their hierarchical structure in the JSON. The Business Agnostic Dataset Catalogue and the Business Agnostic Business Information Base are at the top level, each containing several sub-elements. The Data Objects ABBs are at the same level as these two main elements, indicating their independent but equally important roles in the data architecture. The motivation behind this structure is to provide a comprehensive and flexible framework for managing a wide range of data types and their associated metadata, thereby supporting efficient data operations and business activities.

view.name: SV-Customs Data Models [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The SV-Customs Data Models [Motivation] view extends Semantic view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging the customs data models. This view is composed of three main elements: the "Customs Information Base", the "Customs Data model", and the "Data Model".
The "Customs Information Base" is a Diagram Model-group ABB that encapsulates various Business Object ABBs. These include "Workforce information", "Origin of goods Information", "Internal logistic Information", "Special Procedures Information", "Economic value Information", "Customs partners Information", "Exports information", "Imports information", "Free circulation requirement information", and "Laboratories information". Each of these business objects represents a specific type of information that is crucial for customs operations.
The "Customs Data model" is a Grouping ABB that contains two Data Object SBBs: the "EU Customs Data Model" and the "WCO Data Model". The "EU Customs Data Model" is a standardized framework developed by the European Union for harmonizing and structuring data exchange in customs operations. It promotes data consistency, simplifies data integration, and supports the automation of customs procedures within the EU customs environment. On the other hand, the "WCO Data Model" has been the data foundation for global trade interoperability for over two decades. It provides a universal language for cross-border data exchange, enabling the implementation of Single Window systems and fueling Data Analytics.
Lastly, the "Data Model" is a Data Object ABB that aims to be a collection of entities, their properties, and the relationships among them. It focuses on formally representing a domain, a concept, or a real-world thing.
The motivation behind this view is to provide a comprehensive and structured framework for managing and leveraging customs data. By standardizing and harmonizing the data models, it facilitates interoperability between different customs systems and stakeholders, promotes data consistency, simplifies data integration, and supports the automation of customs procedures. This ultimately leads to reduced costs and improved efficiencies for customs operations.

view.name: SV-Metadata Catalogue [Traceability]
view.documentation: Narrative: The "Semantic view - Metadata Catalogue" extends semantic viewpoint and provides a comprehensive framework for organizing and managing metadata within the digital ecosystem. This view associates the Metadata Catalogue with the Business Information Base and Digital Public Services from the application layer. Within this view, the Metadata Catalogue serves as a centralized repository for storing and categorizing metadata associated with digital assets, resources, and information. It enables efficient discovery, access, and management of metadata, providing essential information about the characteristics, properties, and relationships of digital entities. The Business Information Base, as part of the application layer, relies on the Metadata Catalogue to ensure accurate and meaningful metadata integration and utilization. It utilizes the defined metadata standards and structures to enrich and describe business-related information, supporting data discovery, analysis, and decision-making processes. Digital Public Services leverage the Metadata Catalogue to ensure consistent metadata representation and interoperability among different services. These services align their data models, operations, and interactions with the catalogued metadata, enabling efficient data exchange, integration, and discoverability within the digital ecosystem. By associating the Metadata Catalogue with the Business Information Base and Digital Public Services, the "Semantic view - Metadata Catalogue" promotes standardized metadata management and facilitates its discoverability and reuse. This view ensures consistent metadata representation, improves data quality, and enhances interoperability within the context of digital public services. The catalogued metadata allows for efficient search and retrieval of relevant information, supporting data discovery and analysis. It provides valuable context and insights into the digital assets, facilitating data integration, sharing, and collaboration among different applications and services.

view.name: SV-Customs Datasets [Traceability]
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The SV-Customs Datasets [Motivation] view extends Semantic view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging various elements related to customs data. This view is composed of four main elements: "Customs Dataset Catalogue", "Customs Information Base", "Dataset", and "Customs Dataset Solutions".
The "Customs Dataset Catalogue" is a Grouping ABB that consists of multiple Data Object ABBs. These include "Customs statistical metadata on goods imported", "Applications and Requests metadata", "Laboratory reports index", "Tariffs metadata", "Risk metadata", "Origins metadata", "Cargo metadata", "Declarations metadata", "Intra-EU purchases and sales metadata", "Goods taxonomy metadata", "Notifications metadata", "Procedures metadata", "Customs statistical metadata on goods exported", "Goods metadata", and "Laboratories testing metadata". Each of these data objects represents a specific type of metadata related to customs operations.
The "Customs Information Base" is a Diagram Model-group ABB that contains various Business Object ABBs. These include "Economic Operators Registration and Identification number (EORI)", "Free circulation requirement information", "Laboratories information", "Imports information", "Combined nomenclature", "Special Procedures Information", "Customs partners Information", "Exports information", "Binding Tariffs Information", "Workforce information", "Economic value Information", "Internal logistic Information", "Origin of goods Information", "Guarantee Information", "Classification of goods Information", "Threads and fraudulent actions Information", "Economic Operators Information", "Temporary storage Information", and "Duties calculation Information". Each of these business objects represents a specific type of information related to customs operations.
The "Dataset" is a Data Object ABB that represents a collection of related data organized and presented in a structured format. This element provides a general representation of datasets in the context of customs operations.
The "Customs Dataset Solutions" is a Grouping ABB that includes two Data Object SBBs: "EORI metadata" and "Economic operators metadata". These data objects represent specific types of metadata related to customs dataset solutions.
The relationships between these elements are not explicitly defined in the JSON. However, it can be inferred that the "Customs Dataset Catalogue" and "Customs Dataset Solutions" are related to the "Dataset" as they provide specific types of metadata for datasets. Similarly, the "Customs Information Base" can be related to the "Dataset" as it provides specific types of information that can be included in datasets. The motivation behind these elements and their relationships is to provide a comprehensive and structured representation of customs data, which can be leveraged for various customs operations and solutions.

This view ensures efficient data management, improves data quality, and enhances interoperability within the context of digital public services. The catalogued datasets allow for easy access and retrieval of relevant data, promoting data sharing and collaboration among different applications and services. They enable efficient data integration, reduce redundancy, and support consistent data representation and interpretation.

view.name: SV-Functional Architecture Principles viewpoint
view.documentation:
The view that relates Architecture principles to semantic view functional components is a relevant aspect of solutions architecture. This view focuses on how architecture principles influence the design and implementation of functional components within the semantic layer of a solution.
By aligning architecture principles with semantic view functional components, solutions architects ensure that the design and implementation of these components adhere to established guidelines and best practices. This alignment brings several benefits to the overall solution.
Firstly, it promotes consistency and coherence in the design of functional components. Architecture principles provide guidelines for designing semantic components that ensure a standardized approach and facilitate seamless integration and interoperability. By aligning functional components with these principles, solutions architects ensure that the semantics and data structures across the solution remain consistent, enabling efficient data exchange and integration.
Secondly, aligning architecture principles with semantic view functional components supports data integrity and quality. Architecture principles often emphasize data governance, data security, and data management practices. By incorporating these principles into the design and implementation of semantic components, solutions architects can enforce data governance policies, ensure data security measures, and maintain data quality standards. This alignment enhances the reliability and trustworthiness of the solution's data, leading to more accurate and informed decision-making.
Furthermore, aligning architecture principles with semantic view functional components improves the understandability and maintainability of the solution. Architecture principles provide guidelines for organizing and structuring functional components, making them easier to comprehend and manage. By aligning functional components with these principles, solutions architects facilitate future enhancements, updates, and maintenance of the solution, reducing the complexity and effort required for managing the semantic layer.

view.name: SV-Governance Architecture Principles viewpoint
view.documentation:
The view that relates Architecture principles to semantic view governance components is an essential aspect of solutions architecture. This view specifically focuses on how architecture principles influence the design and implementation of governance structures and processes within the semantic layer of a solution.
Aligning architecture principles with semantic view governance components brings several benefits to the overall solution.
Firstly, it ensures effective governance practices within the semantic layer. Architecture principles provide guidance on establishing governance structures, policies, and processes that govern the management and usage of data. By aligning governance components with these principles, solutions architects can design a robust governance framework that ensures compliance, transparency, and accountability in data management, access control, and data quality. This alignment promotes proper oversight and control over the semantic layer, facilitating efficient and secure data governance practices.
Secondly, aligning architecture principles with semantic view governance components supports data integrity and quality. Architecture principles often emphasize data governance, security, and management best practices. By incorporating these principles into the design and implementation of governance components, solutions architects can establish mechanisms for enforcing data governance policies, implementing security measures, and monitoring data quality. This alignment enhances the reliability and accuracy of data within the semantic layer, contributing to more informed decision-making and reliable business insights.

view.name: SV-Privacy Policy Catalogue
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The SV-Privacy Policy Catalogue view extends Semantic view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging the elements of privacy policy within an organization. This view is composed of several elements, each with a specific role and purpose.
The first element is the 'Privacy Policy', a Business Object ABB. This object regulates the personal data of any customer, client, or employee information. It sets the rules and guidelines for how personal data should be handled, stored, and processed within the organization. It is the cornerstone of the organization's privacy framework, ensuring compliance with data protection laws and regulations.
Nested within the 'Privacy Policy' are two Grouping ABBs: 'Privacy Data Policy Catalogue' and 'Customs Privacy Data Policy Catalogue'. These groupings categorize specific policies related to privacy and data protection.
The 'Privacy Data Policy Catalogue' contains the 'Anonymisation Policy', another Business Object ABB. This policy is a formal document that outlines the rules and procedures for anonymizing sensitive data. It defines the methods, techniques, and criteria used to transform personally identifiable information (PII) into a form that can no longer be linked to an individual. The policy ensures compliance with privacy regulations and helps mitigate the risk of unauthorized disclosure or misuse of personal data. It includes considerations for data anonymization processes, such as data masking, aggregation, or encryption, to protect individuals' privacy while still allowing data to be used for legitimate business purposes.
The 'Customs Privacy Data Policy Catalogue' includes the 'Confidentiality of Business Information', another Business Object ABB. This policy refers to the protection of sensitive and proprietary data belonging to a business or organization. It involves ensuring that confidential information, such as trade secrets, financial data, client lists, and marketing strategies, remains secure and is accessible only to authorized individuals within the organization. Confidentiality safeguards aim to prevent unauthorized access, use, or disclosure of such information, which could compromise the competitive advantage, reputation, or legal standing of the business.
In summary, the SV-Privacy Policy Catalogue view provides a structured and comprehensive framework for managing and implementing privacy policies within an organization. It ensures that all aspects of data privacy, from anonymization to confidentiality, are adequately addressed, thereby safeguarding the organization's data and maintaining compliance with relevant regulations.

view.name: SV-Data Policy Catalogue
view.documentation:
NARRATIVE: The SV-Data Policy Catalogue view extends Semantic view and provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging the Business Agnostic Data Policy Catalogue, which is a Grouping ABB. This catalogue includes several Business Object ABBs, each with its own specific purpose and description.
The first Business Object ABB within the Business Agnostic Data Policy Catalogue is the Interoperability Policy. This policy is a set of guidelines that ensure different systems and data within an organization or across entities work together seamlessly. It promotes the use of open standards and best practices to facilitate smooth communication and integration between various systems, applications, and stakeholders.
The second Business Object ABB is the Data Quality Framework. This framework is a structured approach or set of guidelines that organizations use to assess, measure, and improve the quality of their data. It provides a systematic framework for managing data quality throughout its lifecycle, from data collection to data analysis and decision-making.
The third Business Object ABB is the Data Governance Guidelines. These guidelines are a set of principles, rules, and practices that provide direction and guidance for managing and controlling data assets within an organization. They outline the framework for ensuring data quality, integrity, privacy, security, and compliance throughout the data lifecycle.
The fourth Business Object ABB is the Blockchain policy. This policy is a set of rules, guidelines, and controls that govern the management, access, and utilization of data within a blockchain network or ecosystem. It outlines the specific protocols, procedures, and requirements for storing, validating, and securing data on the blockchain.
Lastly, the Data Policy is a standalone Business Object ABB that aims to form the guiding framework in which data management can operate. This policy is crucial in setting the direction and standards for all data-related activities within an organization.
In summary, the SV-Data Policy Catalogue view provides a comprehensive framework that includes various policies and guidelines to ensure effective data management, interoperability, quality, governance, and security. Each of these elements plays a critical role in managing and controlling data assets, promoting data integrity, privacy, and compliance, and facilitating effective data sharing and collaboration.

view.name: Digital Solution Non-Functional Requirements Catalogue viewpoint
view.documentation:
A non-functional requirements catalog for a digital solution includes a set of criteria and characteristics that describe how the solution should perform, rather than what it should do. These requirements focus on aspects such as performance, security, usability, reliability, and other quality attributes that determine the overall effectiveness and user experience of the solution.
Here are some common categories of non-functional requirements that are often included in such a catalog:
+ Performance: Defines the speed, responsiveness, scalability, and efficiency of the solution under varying conditions, such as user load, data volume, or network latency. + Usability: Specifies the ease of use, intuitiveness, and accessibility of the solution, ensuring that it meets the needs and expectations of its intended users. + Reliability: Addresses the solution's ability to consistently perform its functions accurately and reliably over time, minimizing downtime and data loss. + Security: Covers the protection of data, information, and system resources against unauthorized access, tampering, or breaches. It may include aspects such as authentication, encryption, and compliance with relevant security standards. + Availability: Describes the solution's uptime requirements, including its ability to remain accessible and operational during scheduled maintenance or unexpected outages. + Scalability: Defines the solution's ability to handle increasing workload or user demand by efficiently utilizing resources and adapting to changing circumstances. + Maintainability: Refers to the ease of maintaining and modifying the solution, including aspects such as code maintainability, documentation, and the availability of development and debugging tools. + Interoperability: Specifies the solution's ability to integrate and communicate with other systems or components, often through the use of standardized protocols or interfaces. + Compliance: Ensures that the solution adheres to relevant laws, regulations, and industry standards, such as data protection regulations or accessibility guidelines. + Performance Efficiency: Focuses on optimizing resource usage, minimizing energy consumption, and maximizing the efficiency of the solution's operations. + Testability: Defines the ease with which the solution can be tested to ensure that it meets its functional and non-functional requirements, often through the use of automated testing tools and techniques. + Internationalization and Localization: Addresses the solution's ability to support multiple languages, regions, and cultural conventions to cater to a global user base.
These are just some examples of non-functional requirements that may be included in a catalog for a digital solution. The specific requirements will depend on the nature of the solution, its intended use, and the stakeholders' needs.

view.name: Enterprise Architecture Framework alignment guidelines viewpoint
view.documentation:
The Enterprise Architecture Framework (EAF) alignment guidelines viewpoint serves as an integral part of the process, aiming to establish a harmonious relationship between the European Interoperability Reference Architecture (EIRA) model and any given Enterprise Architecture Framework (EAF). The ultimate goal is to make the EIRA model fully compliant with the chosen EAF, promoting uniformity across the architectural ecosystem.
In this alignment diagram, each Architectural Building Block (ABB) carries a specific connection to the EIRA's Legal, Organisational, Semantic, and Technical (LOST) views that it belongs to. Each ABB forms a critical component of the architecture, representing distinct facets of the EIRA in the broader context of the selected EAF. This viewpoint connects different layers of the enterprise architecture, creating a comprehensive picture of the interoperability landscape.
The intricate ties between each ABB and their corresponding LOST views can be thoroughly explored on the [Properties] sheet under the [Analysis] tab of Archi, a visual modelling and management tool for enterprise architecture. Here, users can investigate each ABB, understanding its role, its relationship with the LOST views, and its part in securing compliance with the EAF.
The EAF alignment guidelines viewpoint allows organizations to align with industry standards, facilitates interoperability, and bridges the EIRA model with the selected EAF. It assists an organization in effectively detailing their enterprise architecture in line with their specific needs while maintaining alignment with larger industry frameworks.
The viewpoint provides a structured layout, enhancing strategic decision-making, facilitating effective communication, and aiding the integration of different architectural elements. This organized alignment fortifies the architecture's robustness and provides a pathway for strategic expansion and evolution.
